segments.he:
ג.
ידוע מאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: בדרך שאדם רוצה לילך מוליכין אותו, ומזה באים כל העצות המקולקלות, שנדמה לו כי מאת השם הם או שהצדיק יעץ לו כך, ובאמת הכל ממנו בעצמו, כמו שכתוב: אולת אדם תסלף דרכו וכו', כי כמו ששואלין את הצדיק, כן הוא משיב על כן מי שרוצה לחוס על עצמו באמת, צריך לבקש מאד בתחנונים רבים את השם יתברך ואת הצדיקי אמת, שישימו לבם היטב על מה שנעשה עמו וירחמו עליו באמת באפן שיתנו לו עצה אמתית, שיצליח על ידה לנצח באמת. (הלכות תענית, הלכה ד', אות ח):
segments.en:
3.
The saying of our Sages of blessed memory is known: "In the path a person wishes to go — he is led along it." And from this come all the corrupted counsels — where it seems to him that they come from G-d — or that the Tzadik gave him this counsel. And in truth it all comes from himself. As it is written: "The folly of a person perverts his way, etc.". For as one asks the Tzadik — so he answers. Therefore one who truly wishes to have consideration for himself must beg greatly in many supplications both G-d, blessed be He, and the truly righteous Tzaddikim — that they place their heart fully upon what is being done with him and have compassion upon him in truth — in a manner that they give him a true counsel through which he will truly succeed forever.

(Hilchos Ta'anis, Halacha 4, item 8).

segments.he: שְׁאָר שַׁבָּת ש ת א ב ר ש
segments.en: Festivals, item 1: inline Hebrew words and letter pairs — שְׁאָר; שַׁבָּת; ש→ת, א→ב, ר→ש.

origin.notice: Editorial identification of inline Hebrew words and letter pairs within Festivals, item 1; the complete teaching is supplied separately.

requiredNotes.text: These words and letters are extracted from Festivals, item 1. Its complete paragraph concerns leaven in the dough and explains the succeeding-letter pairs ש→ת, א→ב, ר→ש, producing תבש, the letters of שבת in reverse. The supplied English prints שְׁאָר with pointing that reads “remainder”; that pointing is preserved, not silently changed. The contextual subject is leaven, not a separate teaching about a remainder.

anchors.text: ש ת א ב ר ש

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The second letters of the word שְׁאָר [she'or — leaven/remnant] are the letters שַׁבָּת [Shabbos] — for after ש [shin] comes ת [tav], and after א [alef] comes ב [bais], and after ר [reish] comes ש [shin] — which are the letters of Shabbos in reverse [l'mafreia]. For the essential nullification of chametz [leaven] and she'or [sourdough] in the dough — which is the yetzer hara that obstructs [one] from doing His blessed will, and is the aspect of the other god [ail acher], forced apostasy [shmad], G-d forbid — the essential nullification is through the holiness of Shabbos. For then the metzach haratzon [the forehead of will] is revealed — the aspect of ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills]. And from there the Tzadik draws the supreme encompassing redemption [pidyon elyon hakolel] — until he nullifies the she'or aforementioned and elevates [one] from shmad to ratzon [will].

segments.he:
ד.
לפעמים נופל האדם לספקות ועצות חלוקות כל כך, כד שאי אפשר לו בשום אפן לידע האמת איך להתנהג, וכל מה שחותר למצא עצה שלמה, מבלבלין עצתו בכל פעם כי עכשו נגמר בדעתו בראיות ברורות, שהוא צריך להתנהג כך, ובתוך כך עולה על דעתו סברא אחרת, עד שעצתו הראשונה נסתרת לגמרי, ועולים סברות בדעתו שצריך להתנהג בהפוך ממש ממה שחשב מקדם, וזה בחינת עצות חלוקות הנ"ל. ולפעמים מתגבר חלוקת העצה כל כך, עד שאינו יודע בשום אפן להכריע העצה לכאן או לכאן, וכשהאדם רואה בעצמו, שהוא מונח בחשך זה זמן רב ואינו יודע שום עצה איך לצאת ממה שצריך לצאת, ועצתו חלוקה מאד, חס ושלום, אזי זהו בעצמו תקנתו, שיצעק על זה בעצמו להשם יתברך על אשר נפל כל כך, עד שאינו יודע העצה שלמה איך לצאת מחשך לאור, כי בודאי אין שום יאוש בעולם כלל, ובודאי גם במקומו נמצאין עצות איך לצאת מחשך לאור, מרע לטוב, רק שבעוונותיו נעלמו ממנו העצות בבחינת: מי זה מחשיך עצה במילין וכו', ועל כן תקנתו, שידע על כל פנים האמת, שנפל כל כך ונתרחק כל כך עד שאינו יודע שום עצה, ויצעק על זה בעצמו להשם יתברך, שיורהו העצה והדרך איך להתנהג באמת, וכמו שדוד המלך, עליו השלום צעק על זה הרבה, כי באמת גם על הצדיקים הגדולים במעלה מאד עוברים עליהם גם כן עצות עצות חלוקות בעניניהם ובהנהגותיהם, וכמובן במה שצעק דוד המלך, עליו השלום: עד אנה אשית עצות בנפשי וכו', שמובן מזה, שעברו עליו חלוקות העצה הרבה מאד, מכל שכן וכל שכן קטני הערך, מכל שכן הנלכדים במאסר התאוות ובהרהורים וכו' וכו', רחמנא לצלן, שצריכין לידע ולהאמין, שבודאי בכל מקום שהם יש שם עצה ותחבולה איך לצאת ולשוב משם, אך שאין יודעין העצה, ועצתם חלוקה תמיד, על כן תקנתם - שידעו האמת, שאין יודעים שום עצה, ויתפללו על זה הרבה להשם יתברך, ואז יכולין לזכות שתהיה הירידה תכלית העליה, כמבאר בפנים, (הלכות גטין, הלכה ג', אות כה):
segments.en:
4.
Sometimes a person falls into so many doubts and divided counsels — that it is impossible for him in any way to know the truth as to how to conduct himself. And everything he strives to find as a complete counsel — his counsel is confused every single time. For now he has concluded in his mind with clear proofs that he must conduct himself in such and such a manner. And in the meanwhile a different view arises in his mind — until his first counsel is entirely overturned. And there arise in his mind views that he must conduct himself in the complete opposite of what he had previously thought. And this is the aspect of the divided counsels aforementioned. And sometimes the division of counsel intensifies so greatly — that he does not know in any way to decide the counsel to one side or the other.

And when a person sees in himself that he has been lying in this darkness for a long time and does not know any counsel as to how to emerge from what he needs to emerge from — and his counsel is very divided, G-d forbid — then this itself is his remedy: that he cry out to G-d, blessed be He, about this very thing itself — about having fallen so far that he does not know the complete counsel as to how to emerge from darkness to light. For certainly there is no despair in the world at all. And certainly even in his place there are counsels as to how to emerge from darkness to light, from bad to good. Only that through his sins they have been hidden from him — in the aspect of: "Who is this who darkens counsel with words, etc.?". And therefore his remedy is: that he know at least the truth — that he has fallen so far and been distanced so far that he does not know any counsel. And let him cry out about this itself to G-d, blessed be He — that He show him the counsel and the path as to how to truly conduct himself. As King David, peace be upon him, cried out much about this — for in truth even the very great Tzaddikim of very high stature — even upon them there pass — [counsels] — divided counsels in their matters and in their conduct. And as is understood from what King David, peace be upon him, cried out: "How long shall I take counsel in my soul, etc.?" — from which it is understood that greatly divided counsels passed over him. How much more so and certainly those of lower worth — how much more so those caught in the prison of desires and improper thoughts, etc. etc., G-d protect us — who must know and believe that certainly in every place they are, there is a counsel and a strategy as to how to emerge and return from there. Only they do not know the counsel — and their counsel is always divided. And therefore their remedy is: that they know the truth — that they do not know any counsel — and pray about this much to G-d, blessed be He. And then they can merit that the descent become the ultimate ascent, as explained in the inner teachings.

(Hilchos Gittin, Halacha 3, item 25).

history.en: The essential blemish of faith in the sages comes from those who dispute the truly wise sages — because they are wise in their own eyes in the futile wisdoms of this world, all of which are wisdoms of falsehood — since through these wisdoms one does not merit the true and eternal purpose. And in truth the root of all these wisdoms — whether the outright external wisdoms of the philosophical investigators, or the ordinary wisdoms of the world that are against the point of truth — all derive solely from the fact that their entire intention is only for the sake of the bodily desires. Which is the aspect of weekday eating [achilas chol], where the liver is nourished first and afterwards the brain. And through the holiness of the delight of Shabbos [oneg Shabbos] — when the brain is nourished first — through this — [through this] — all the aforementioned disputants are subdued, and the faith in the sages is repaired.

segments.he: ערך צדיק
segments.en: Tzadik

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The greatness of the commandment of the Kiddush Levanah [sanctification of the new moon] is very precious — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And it alludes to the renewal of the world in the time to come — for Israel is destined to be renewed like it. And since the essential faith in the renewal of the world is drawn through the prayer of the [Tzadik who is the] ba'al ko'ach [master of power] — through which the clouds, which are the sitra achra, dissolve and are gone in the aspect of: "I have wiped away your transgressions like a cloud, etc." [Isaiah 44:22] — as explained in the inner teachings — therefore the moon may only be sanctified when the clouds are not covering it.

segments.he:
א.
צריכין לנדד שנה מעיניו ומעפעפיו - תנומה לשוטט ולבקש ולהרבות בתפלה ותחנונים, שיזכה למצא הצדיק, שיוכל לרפאתו ולהכניס בו השגת אלקות ולהציל את נפשו מני שחת, ועל זה צריכין לשבר השנה ולקום בחצות לילה ולבכות ולצעק מאד על חורבן בית המקדש ועל הסתלקות הצדיקים, שקשה כפלים כחורבן בית המקדש, עד שיזכה גם עתה למצא הרבי והמנהיג האמתי, האמתי, שיוכל להכניס בו ידיעת אלקותו יתברך, שעל ידי זה יתמלאו לו כל החסרונות ויתבטלו כל הצרות ויתתקן הכל. (הלכות השכמת הבקר, הלכה ד', אות ז):
segments.en:
1.
One must banish sleep from his eyes and slumber from his eyelids — to wander and seek and multiply prayer and supplication, that he merit to find the Tzadik who can heal him and bring within him the attainment of G-dliness, and rescue his soul from destruction. And for this one must break the sleep and rise at midnight and weep and cry out greatly over the destruction of the Temple and over the passing of the Tzaddikim — which is twice as hard as the destruction of the Temple. Until he merits even now to find the true — [true] — rebbe and leader, who can bring within him the knowledge of His blessed G-dliness. Through which all his lacks will be filled and all afflictions nullified and everything repaired.

(Hilchos Hashkomas HaBoker, Halacha 4, item 7).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: But regarding those who are meticulous not to sanctify it even when it is visible through a thin and light cloud — all of this is out of great love for the commandment, wishing it to be completely clear and pure. But they did not intend well in this. For in this low and dark world — especially now, in these generations, when the sitra achra has spread very greatly — if we wish to be so meticulous in all the commandments and wait until we can fulfill them with great clarity and purity and brightness, especially with the purity of thought which is the essential — then all the Torah and commandments would already be nullified, G-d forbid. And in truth we must fulfill all the commandments as best we can. And only through this do we keep ourselves alive in this bitter exile — in the very slightest light that shines upon us from within the depth of this very darkness and gloom. And if we wish to be scrupulous and stringent with excessive stringencies — we could stumble and fall through this even more, G-d forbid. Therefore certainly, far be it from us to withhold from the commandment of Kiddush Levanah on account of the aforementioned scrupulosities. Rather, we must fulfill it as our Sages of blessed memory said in the Gemara and the Poskim — that one is obligated to sanctify it even when it is visible through a thin cloud. Especially when the time is pressed and close to the end of the time for sanctification. Especially in winter.

segments.he:
ב.
הצדיק הגדול הנ"ל, שעוסק לקרב הרחוקים, שנאחז בהם הבעל דבר וחילותיו ביותר, הוא בעצם חכמתו מוריד את עצמו כל כך אליהם, עד שנדמה כאלו עושה מעשה נערות, כי מדבר עמהם שיחות חולין ואוכל ושותה עמהם ולפעמים מטיל ומשחק עמהם, וכל כונתו -כדי לקרבם על ידי זה להשם יתברך. (שם, אות טז):
segments.en:
2.
The great Tzadik aforementioned — who engages in drawing close those who are distant, in whom the baal davar and his forces have seized with greatest force — descends in the very depth of his wisdom so far toward them, until it appears as if he is performing acts of youthfulness. For he speaks mundane conversation with them and eats and drinks with them — and sometimes walks about and plays with them. And all his intention — to draw them close to G-d, blessed be He, through this.

(ibid., item 16).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The twelve lunar months correspond to the twelve versions of the prayer [nuscha'os hatefilah] — corresponding to the twelve tribes. And the leap month is corresponding to the tribe of Yosef — who was divided into two tribes. And the essential purpose of the leap [ibur] is to align the solar years with the lunar years — that is, to join the twelve tribes, which are the aspect of the twelve versions of the prayer, to the aspect of Yaakov — who is the aspect of the very substance of truth, the aspect of the sun [chamah]. And through this comes the essential perfection of the prayer.

segments.he:
ג.
מעלה גדולה להיות אצל הצדיק בזמן שיש אצלו קבוץ גדול מהרבה אנשים מישראל, כי בודאי כל אחד ואחד בפרט הוא רחוק הרבה מאד מקדושת הצדיק הדור, ואי אפשר לקבל ממנו רק על ידי כלליות ישראל, שעל ידי זה נמשכת הארתו הגדולה, ואז יכול גם כל אחד ואחד לקבל הארתו בפרטיות. (הלכות תפלין, הלכה ב', אות ד):
segments.en:
3.
There is great virtue in being with the Tzadik at a time when there is a large gathering of many people of Israel with him. For certainly every single particular person is very, very far from the holiness of the Tzadik of the generation. And it is impossible to receive [illumination] from him except through the collective of Israel — through which his great illumination is drawn. And then every single particular person can also receive his illumination individually.

(Hilchos Tefillin, Halacha 2, item 4).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Through being careful about chametz for seven days and eating matzah — through this the da'as [knowledge/awareness] of faith in Providence is revealed. Until one knows in truth that even nature itself — which is the aspect of chametz — also conducts itself solely through His blessed Providence. For G-d created everything and governs everything through His will. And therefore afterwards eating chametz is also permitted.

segments.he:
ד.
מה שמועיל תשובה לכל החטאים, הוא רק מצד החסד ועל עוון הוצאת זרע לבטלה אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, שאין מועיל לו תשובה, כי כך ראוי לו, כמבאר בפנים אבל באמת אין לך דבר, שעומד בפני התשובה, אך עקר תקונו הוא על ידי הצדיק הדור, כי הוא יכול לעורר ולהמשיך עליו חסד חדש, עד שיתתקן גם כן. (שם, אות יא):
segments.en:
4.
That teshuvah is effective for all sins — this is only from the side of chesed [kindness]. And for the sin of wasting seed [hotzo'as zera l'vatolo] our Sages of blessed memory said that teshuvah is not effective for it — for such is fitting for it, as explained in the inner teachings. But in truth there is nothing that stands before teshuvah. Only the essential repair is through the Tzadik of the generation. For he can awaken and draw upon him new chesed — until this too will be repaired.

(ibid., item 11).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: A person must remember very — [very] — well all the days of his life, each and every day, the day he departed from the land of Egypt — as it is written: "So that you will remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt, etc." [Deuteronomy 16:3]. That is: how he departed from Egypt before the appointed time, only through His kindness — and because of this, what passes over him now passes over him. For in every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt. For all of the above passes over every person. And therefore one must remember each and every day the greatness of His blessed kindness — that He brought him out from where He brought him out, which is the aspect of the exodus from Egypt. And even though now what passes over him passes over him — even so, certainly the kindness and goodness that G-d has done with him is certainly not in vain, G-d forbid. Rather, he must now pass through these matters and be tested through them. But in the end G-d will complete His part — and he will merit to draw close to His blessed service and to find all his losses in perfection. For the word of our G-d endures forever.

segments.he:
ה.
בכל דור ודור יש כמה צדיקים אמתיים, אבל יש אמת למעלה מאמת, כי בודאי אין מדרגת כל הצדיקים שוין, וכל מה שמעלת ומדרגת הצדיקים גדול יותר, בודאי האמת שלו גדול ומברר ביותר, כי העקר הוא האמת, עד שיש בכל דור צדיק אמתי, שהוא בחינת נקודת האמת שבין הצדיקים, רק מחמת התגברות החלופים והתמורות, על ידי זה קשה מאד לידע היכן האמת, כי על פי רב מתגרה הבעל דבר בהצדיקים בעצמן ומכניס ביניהם מחלקת גדול לחלק על זה הצדיק האמת, שהוא בחינת נקודת האמת שבין הצדיקים, ונדמה להם כאלו זה הצדיק דיקא נוטה, חס ושלום, מדרך האמת, ומזה היה בחינת המחלקת שחלקו השבטים על יוסף, עד אשר לעבד נמכר יוסף, ועל ידי זה נתגלגל הדבר וירדו אבותינו למצרים והיו שם עבדים, וכן מחלקת שאול, שרדף את דוד בחנם, וכמו שמצינו בכמה וכמה דורות, בפרט בדורות הללו בעקבות משיחא, שהתגבר הקטגוריא והמחלקת גם בין הצדיקים, עד שאין יודעים היכן האמת, על כן צריכין להתפלל להשם יתברך על זה הרבה כנ"ל. (הלכות ברכות השחר, הלכה ג', אות יז):
segments.en:
5.
In every generation there are many truly righteous Tzaddikim. But there is truth above truth — for certainly the level and stature of all Tzaddikim is not equal. And the greater the stature and level of the Tzaddikim — certainly his truth is greater and more fully clarified. For the essential thing is truth. Until in every generation there is a true Tzadik who is the aspect of the point of truth among the Tzaddikim. Only because of the intensification of the substitutions and exchanges — through this it is very difficult to know where the truth is. For most of the time the baal davar provokes even the Tzaddikim themselves and introduces great controversy between them — to dispute this true Tzadik who is the aspect of the point of truth among the Tzaddikim. And it seems to them as if this specific Tzadik is the one who deviates, G-d forbid, from the path of truth.

And from this came the aspect of the controversy of the tribes against Yosef — until "as a slave was Yosef sold". And through this the matter rolled on, and our ancestors descended to Egypt and were slaves there. And likewise the controversy of Shaul — who pursued David for no cause. And as we find in many, many generations. Especially in these generations in the footsteps of the Mashiach — when the accusation and the controversy intensified even among the Tzaddikim — until one does not know where the truth is. And therefore one must pray to G-d, blessed be He, much about this as above.

(Hilchos Bircas HaShachar, Halacha 3, item 17).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The essential redemption depends on faith [emunah]. And to complete faith, it is impossible to merit except through truth. And to come to truth is through receiving the holy counsels of the truly righteous Tzaddikim. And this is the aspect of the totality of the Torah — the 613 counsels of the Torah [taryag itin d'oraisa]. And this is the aspect of the great miracle of the exodus from Egypt. For at that time it was still before the giving of the Torah — which is those 613 counsels aforementioned. For since the defilements of Egypt still clung to them very greatly — therefore it was still impossible for them to receive the light of the holy counsels. Because of the defilement of the serpent — which is the aspect of the counsel of the wicked — that still clung to them. And naturally, when one does not merit to receive the light of the holy counsels — then one is distant from truth and from faith. And how can there be a redemption?!

segments.he:
ו.
תקון זה, שעוסק הצדיק בחינת משה להעלות משמד לרצון, זה צריך גם כל אחד לפי מדרגתו, כי אפלו הכשרים, כשסרים לפעמים מאחרי השם יתברך, נחשב לעבודה זרה בחינת שמד, רחמנא לצלן, בחינת: וסרתם ועבדתם אלהים אחרים, כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה. ועקר בחינת עבודה זרה ושמד הוא בחינת תאות ממון וטרדת ומרירת הפרנסה, שהשטן והבעל דבר מפיל את כל אחד בדעתו לטבעיות ורוצה להרחיקו מאמונת ההשגחה והרצון העליון, ומחמת זה דואג תמיד על ממון ופרנסה, ויש שיש לו ממון הרבה ומתאוה יותר ויותר, וכל זה הוא בחינת שמד, כי כל העבודות זרות תחובים בממון, כמבאר במקום אחר והתקון לזה - לקשר את עצמו לצדיקי הדור האמתיים בחינת משה ולהרבות בצדקה דקדושה לשם שמים, ולא להתפאר, חס ושלום, ועל ידי זה ממשיכים הארת הרצון מבחינת משה, שנסתלק, ונכלל בשרש הרצון רעוא דרעוין, עד שעל ידי זה יאיר להם הרצון דקדושה בכל מיני חשך להעלותם משם, משם, שעל ידי זה עולין משמד לרצון. (שם, הלכה ה', אות מה, סא):
segments.en:
6.
This repair that the Tzadik — in the aspect of Moshe — engages in: to elevate from forced apostasy [shmad] to will [ratzon] — this is also needed by every single person according to his level. For even the upright — when they sometimes turn away from G-d, blessed be He — this is considered idol worship [avodah zarah] in the aspect of shmad, G-d protect us. As our Sages of blessed memory said regarding: "And you will turn away and serve other gods". And the essential aspect of idolatry and shmad is the desire for money and the entanglement and bitterness of livelihood. For the adversary and the baal davar brings down each person's mind to naturalism [tiv'iyus] — and wishes to distance him from faith in Providence and the Supreme Will. And because of this one always worries about money and livelihood. And there are those who have much money and desire more and more. And all of this is the aspect of shmad. For all idol worship is embedded in money, as explained elsewhere.

And the repair for this is to bind oneself to the truly righteous Tzaddikim of the generation — in the aspect of Moshe — and to multiply in holy tzedakah for the sake of Heaven, and not to be boastful, G-d forbid. And through this the illumination of the will is drawn from the aspect of Moshe who has departed — and is encompassed in the root of the will — ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills]. Until through this the holy will shines upon them in every kind of darkness to elevate them from there — [from there] — so that through this they ascend from shmad to ratzon.

(ibid., Halacha 5, items 45, 61).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And G-d made His kindness wondrous to us — and shined upon us a great and very awesome light that was not in a gradual manner. That is, He shined upon us the light of the very essence of truth before we merited to receive the holy counsels. And through the light of truth we merited great faith — through which the redemption came. And this is the aspect of the great and awesome expanded consciousness [moichin gedolim v'nora'im] alluded to in the commandment of eating matzah — that is, the aspect of the greatness of the illumination of the very essence of truth that shines upon us then. For the essential purpose of the greatness of the expanded consciousness is truth — which is the sum total of all the holy expanded consciousnesses in the world. And therefore chametz is then forbidden with a severe prohibition. For a person's eating corresponds to da'as — for the brain and the da'as are commensurate with the eating. As explained elsewhere. And all the holy counsels are the aspect of the leavening of the holy brain [chamitz hamoi'ach d'kedushah] — for counsel must be [developed] with settled mind and deliberateness, until the matter is well leavened. But corresponding to this there is also the aspect of the leavening of the brain of the sitra achra — which are evil counsels and thoughts and bad ideas that are against the holy Torah. And therefore the yetzer hara is called the she'or sheba'isah [the leaven in the dough]. And there is no wisdom and no counsel to stand against it — except through the holy counsels of the holy Torah. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "I created the yetzer hara — I created the Torah as its antidote."

segments.he:
ז.
זה ידוע לכל אדם כמה וכמה עתים עוברים עליו ברוחניות וגשמיות בגוף ונפש וממון וכו', וכמה וכמה ישועות נפלאות שהשם יתברך עוזר לו בכל פעם, בפרט בענין קדושת יהדותו, שזהו העקר. ובכל עת ועת שעובר על האדם, בין בטיבו בין בעקו, בין בעליה בין בירידה - בכולם מאיר בהם הצדיק, שידעו ישראל עצות מה לעשות ובמה יחיה את עצמו בכל עת ועת כפי העת אשר עובר עליו, באפן שישארו על עמדם ולא יפלו ולא יתרחקו לעולם. והעקר - על ידי שיקשרו כל העתים העוברים עליהם לעת האחרון, שהוא עת קבול השכר של כל אחד מישראל, שאז יזכה כל אחד כפי עבודתו להארת הרצון המופלג להשם יתברך בהשתוקקות נפלא ונורא, שזה בחינת: כעת יאמר ליעקב ולישראל מה פעל אל, כמבאר בפנים, ולעת הזאת צריכין לקשר כל העתים העוברים עליו בעולם הזה, כי עקר ההתחזקות הוא על ידי הרצון, שאיך שהוא ואיך שעובר עליו, על כל פנים יחזק את עצמו ברצון חזק להשם יתברך, כי הרצון הטוב בעצמו יקר וחשוב מאד, ועל ידי זה יתעורר ויתגבר להתפלל תמיד להשם יתברך ולהרבות באמירת תהלים ותחנות ובקשות רבות והתבודדות לשפך לבו כמים לפני השם, עד ישקיף וירא השם משמים ויאיר עליו הדעת הקדוש האמתי לבטל הרוח שטות ולשוב מכל העוונות ולהתקרב להשם יתברך. (הלכות נטילת ידים לסעודה, הלכה ו', אות נא):
segments.en:
7.
Every person well knows — how many and how many times pass over him — spiritually and physically — in body and soul and money, etc. And with how many and how many wondrous salvations G-d, blessed be He, helps him each and every time. Especially in the matter of the holiness of his Judaism — which is the essential thing. And at every time and every time that passes over a person — whether in good or in hardship, whether in ascent or in descent — through all of them the Tzadik illuminates, so that Israel know what counsels to take and by what to keep themselves alive at every time — each according to the time that passes over him. In a manner that they will remain standing and will never fall or be distanced.

And the essential [means] is: through binding all the times that pass over them to the last time — which is the time of receiving the reward of every person of Israel. At that time every person will merit according to his service the illumination of an overflowing will toward G-d, blessed be He — with a wondrous and awesome yearning. Which is the aspect of: "As now it will be said of Yaakov and of Israel: what has G-d wrought?" — as explained in the inner teachings. And to this time one must bind all the times that pass over him in this world. For the essential strengthening is through the will [ratzon] — that however things are and whatever passes over him — at the very least he should strengthen himself with a strong will toward G-d, blessed be He. For the good will in itself is very precious and important. And through this he will be awakened and will strengthen himself to always pray to G-d, blessed be He, and to multiply the recitation of Psalms and supplications and many requests and hisbodidus — to pour out his heart like water before G-d — until G-d looks down from Heaven and sees — and shines upon him the true holy da'as to nullify the spirit of folly and to return from all sins and to draw close to G-d, blessed be He.

(Hilchos Netilas Yodayim L'seudah, Halacha 6, item 51).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And since at that time it was still before the receiving of the Torah — and it was impossible to wait until they received the light of truth through the holy counsels in a gradual and orderly manner, because the defilement of the serpent — which is the aspect of the counsel of the wicked — still clung to them — therefore chametz and she'or were then forbidden. For then the chametz is the aspect of the leavening of the brain of the sitra achra. Rather, we must receive then the light of truth itself — before it is leavened and clothed in the aspect of counsels. And therefore on Shavuos — when we merited to receive the 613 counsels and the defilement of the serpent ceased from us — then the chametz was sweetened and repaired with great holiness, to the point that specifically then two loaves of leavened bread [shtai halechem] are brought.

segments.he:
ח.
עקר היצר הרע, שמתגבר בכל דור ודור, הוא להסתיר ולהעלים את הצדיק האמת שבדור הזה דיקא, כנראה בחוש, שעקר המחלקת - על הצדיק שבאותו הדור, ואחר כך, בשכבר הימים הבאים, מודים העולם גם בזה הצדיק ואומרים, שזה בודאי היה צדיק, רק שחולקים על זה הצדיק שבאותו הדור, כמו שראינו בענין המחלקת שהיה על האר"י זכרונו לברכה, בימיו, ואחר כך הודו כולם בקדושת האר"י וחלקו על הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה,ו וכן בכל דור. וכל זה - מחמת שעקר ברור המדמה, שעל ידי זה זוכין לאמונה שלמה, הוא דיקא על ידי זה הצדיק האמת שבדור הזה דיקא. ועל כן מניח עצמו הבעל דבר לארכו ולרחבו להסתיר ולהעלים זה הצדיק דיקא, ועל כן צריך כל אחד להשתדל ולהתקרב לצדיק האמת שבדור הזה דיקא, כדי שיזכה על ידו דיקא לשלמות ברור האמונה שצריכין כפי אותו הדור והעת והזמן של עכשו דיקא. (הלכות ברכות הריח, הלכה ד', אות לג)
segments.en:
8.
The essential [work of the] yetzer hara — which intensifies in every generation — is to hide and conceal the true Tzadik of this very generation. As is plainly visible: the essential controversy is against the Tzadik of that very generation. And afterwards — in the days that come — the world acknowledges also this Tzadik and says that he was certainly a Tzadik. Only they dispute the Tzadik of this very generation. As we saw regarding the controversy that existed against the Arizal, of blessed memory, in his own days — and afterwards all acknowledged the holiness of the Arizal and disputed the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory — and so in every generation. And all of this — because the essential clarification [birur] of the imagination — through which one merits complete faith — is specifically through this very true Tzadik of this very generation.

And therefore the baal davar exerts itself fully to hide and conceal this specific Tzadik. And therefore every person must strive and draw close to the true Tzadik of this very generation — specifically. In order to merit through him specifically the perfection of the clarification of faith — as is needed for this very generation and time and moment — specifically now.

(Hilchos Bircas HaReach, Halacha 4, item 33).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this matter of the exodus from Egypt occurs in every person and at every time. For whenever a person is sunk, G-d forbid, in the exile of the soul — there are times when a person is so sunken that it is impossible to reveal to him any holy counsel as to how to emerge from the darkness and the exile. For whatever holy counsel may be given to him — the sitra achra overpowers it and corrupts it through its evil counsels — which are the aspect of the defilement of the serpent. But when G-d has compassion upon a person and wishes to bring within him an awakening to teshuvah — then G-d illuminates in his mind the light of the very essence of truth before the holy counsels are revealed. Through this very truth he is drawn after holiness with great yearning and merits faith. And through this he draws close to the truly righteous Tzaddikim and walks in the path of their counsel. And then he receives the true truth of the true Tzadik and of the holy Torah — through receiving the holy counsels within which the light of truth is clothed. For the counsel of the Tzaddikim is the aspect of "all of it seed of truth."

segments.he:
ט.
מי שמפריד את עצמו מהצדיק, הוא בחינת עץ יבש, כי אף על פי שמחדש איזה חדוש בתורה, אינו נחשב בשם עשית פרות כלל, כי אי אפשר להצליח בתורה ולעשות פרות באמת, כי אם כשמקשרין את עצמו להצדיק האמת, שעל ידי זה זוכין לכסופין טובים ולמעשים טובים ולחדושי תורה אמתיים. (הלכות הודאה, הלכה ה', אות ח):
segments.en:
9.
One who separates himself from the Tzadik — he is the aspect of a dry tree [etz yaveish]. For even if he innovates some innovation in Torah — it is not considered the making of fruit at all. For it is impossible to succeed in Torah and to make true fruit — except when one binds oneself to the true Tzadik. Through which one merits good longings, and good deeds, and true Torah innovations.

(Hilchos Hodaah, Halacha 5, item 8).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this too is the aspect of eating maror [bitter herbs] — which is in remembrance of the subjugation and exile. For one must endure great bitterness before meriting to extract the holy counsels from the grip of the sitra achra — which is the aspect of the counsel of the serpent — that confuses all the holy counsels and literally makes life bitter. Which is the aspect of: "And they made their lives bitter with mortar and with bricks" [Exodus 1:14] — b'chomra d'shme'ata ulivun halachta [in the difficulty of the studied law and the clarification of the halacha] — for all of this is the aspect of the extraction and clarification of the holy counsels, which are the sum total of all the halachos in the Torah — the 613 counsels. And it is called counsel and wisdom [etzah v'sushiyah]. But through the illumination of the very essence of truth that G-d shined upon us at Pesach — through this all the aforementioned bitterness was nullified through the illumination of the great expanded consciousness — the aspect of the light of truth — which is the aspect of matzah as above.

segments.he:
י.
מי שרוצה לחוס על חייו, להציל נפשו ממיתה עולמית ולהנצל מסטרא דמותא, שהוא בחינת כפירות, ולזכות לאמונה שלמה, שהיא עקר החיים, צריך לנסע ולבוא אל הצדיקים והנלוים אליהם, שזה סוד ארבעים ושמונה ערי מקלט, שישבו בהם הכהנים והלויים, שהיה צריך הרוצח לנוס ולברח לשם, וארבעים ושמונה ערים אלו הם כנגד ארבעים ושמונה תבות שבפרשת שמע ישראל, שהוא יסוד האמונה הקדושה. (הלכות תחומין, הלכה ה', אות לז):
segments.en:
10.
One who wishes to have consideration for his life — to rescue his soul from eternal death — and to be saved from the aspect of death [sitra d'musa], which is the aspect of heresies [kefirot] — and to merit complete faith, which is the very essence of life — must journey and come to the Tzaddikim and those attached to them. Which is the secret of the forty-eight cities of refuge [arei miklat] — in which the priests and the Levites dwelt. And where the killer was required to flee and escape. And these forty-eight cities correspond to the forty-eight words of the passage of Shma Yisroel — which is the foundation of the holy faith.

(Hilchos Techumin, Halacha 5, item 37).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Wine elevates the mind above its level. And therefore there are two aspects to it: if one is worthy [zachah] — it becomes a head [rosh]; if not worthy — it becomes impoverished [rash]. For it is impossible to drink wine in great holiness except when one merits the repair of the bris — through which one merits holy counsels and truth and faith. And then one can merit through the wine — that his brain will be elevated and his da'as expanded, until he ascends to the root of da'as: which is the aspect of the root of Torah and commandments — where he is above all the commandments of the Torah. And all the commandments receive their vitality and illumination from there. And when he ascends there, he is inflamed more and more and strengthened more and more to fulfill the commandments of the Torah — because he draws upon himself the light of the root of the commandments.

segments.he:
יא.
אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: עשה לך רב וקנה לך חבר. ומובא בספרים, שמרמז על הקנה והקולמוס, שכותבין בו הספרים הקדושים. וזה: עשה לך רב - ואם אינך יכול למצאו, אזי התקון על ידי וקנ"ה לך חבר, הינו על ידי הספרים הקדושים הנכתבים בקנה, תחבר אותם אליך אליך ותעין בהם היטב, ועל ידי זה תוכל לידע מי הרב האמת. (הלכות ראש חדש, הלכה ז', אות נה):
segments.en:
11.
Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend." And it is brought in the sacred books that this alludes to the reed [kaneh] and the quill [kulmus] with which the holy books are written. And this: "Make for yourself a teacher" — and if you cannot find him, then the remedy is through: "and acquire for yourself a friend" — that is, through the holy books written with a reed [kaneh] — bind them to yourself — to yourself and study them well. And through this you will be able to know who is the true teacher.

(Hilchos Rosh Chodesh, Halacha 7, item 55).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

requiredNotes.text: The wording plays on acquiring a friend and the reed used for writing, קנ"ה. The Hebrew repeats אליך (“to yourself”), not the verb; the English repeats “to yourself” accordingly.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: But in the reverse, G-d forbid — when one has not yet merited the aforementioned aspects, and his faith is not yet complete — then through the drinking of wine and intoxication one can greatly corrupt — to the point that all evil paths seem to him like a plain, G-d forbid. As it is written: "For he sets his eye upon the cup — he walks in upright paths" [Proverbs 23:31] — meaning: seemingly straight to him. For since his brain has been elevated above the vessels of his own brain — he no longer sees according to his own level all the warnings of the commandments of Moshe — [Moshe] — our master. And as is explained elsewhere on the verse: "Lest he drink and forget what has been decreed" [Proverbs 31:5].

segments.he:
יב.
מעלת קברי הצדיקים - כי הם שוכני עפר, שגם בחייהם נעשים שכנים לעפר, כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, ועל ידי זה יש להם בחינת כח המושך שיש להעפר, הינו שיש להם כח להמשיך אצלם קדושת אלקותו יתברך ולהמשיך כל העולם אל קדושת עבודתו יתברך, ומכל שכן עתה, אחר ההסתלקות, שהם שוכני עפר ממש, ואז במקום קבורת הצדיק, שם העפר הוא בחינת עפר ארץ ישראל, אדמת קדש, בבחינת: צדיקים יירשו ארץ, כמבאר במקום אחר, ועל כן בנקל להתעורר שם באמת לעבודתו יתברך ולהגביר הכח המושך דקדושה על הכח המכריח. (הלכות יום טוב, הלכה ה', אות ב):
segments.en:
12.
The virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for they are dwellers of the dust [shochnei ofor]. Who even in their lifetimes made themselves neighbors to dust — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And through this they have the aspect of the drawing power that dust has — that is, they have the power to draw toward themselves the holiness of His blessed G-dliness and to draw the entire world toward the holiness of His blessed service. And how much more so now — after the passing — when they are literally dwellers of the dust. And then at the place of the burial of the Tzadik — the dust there is in the aspect of the dust of the Land of Israel — holy soil [admas kodesh]. In the aspect of: "the righteous shall inherit the land" — as explained elsewhere. And therefore it is easy to truly awaken there to His blessed service — and to strengthen the drawing power of holiness over the compelling power.

(Hilchos Yom Tov, Halacha 5, item 2).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore at Pesach — when the light of truth itself is revealed above the level of the expanded consciousness — that is, before truth is clothed in the counsels as above — therefore the obligation is to drink four cups of wine. For now, specifically through the wine, the brain is elevated and one receives the light of truth itself above the vessels of the expanded consciousness. And through this the holy faith is completed. And through this the blemish of Adam the first is repaired — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "She squeezed grapes and gave it to him." And the blemish of Noach — as it is said of him: "And he drank of the wine, etc." — as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he:
יג.
גדל מעלת קברי הצדיקים - כי שם יכולין הכל להתתקן, אפלו מי שהוא בין שני הס"מ, חס ושלום, יכול הצדיק הגדול להוציאו משם, כשבאים על קברו הקדוש ורוצה לחזר בתשובה שלמה, כי מיתת הצדיק הגדול גבוה ונעלה ונשגב מאד, ואז דיקא הוא מתגבר בכל כחו לגמר מה שצריך לגמר לטובת נפשות ישראל, כי מיתת הצדיק הוא בחינת תפלה בבחינת דין, שמתפלל הבעל כח הגדול והסטרא אחרא בולעת אותה, והתפלה מחמת שהיא קדושה מאד ויצאה מבעל כח גדול, על כן אין כח להסטרא אחרא לבלע אותה לגמרי, רק אדרבא, התפלה עומדת לה בצוארה, עד שהסטרא אחרא מוכרחת על ידי זה להקיא ולהוציא ולהחזיר כל הקדושות שבלעה, אף גם עצמות חיותה ממש. וזה סוד התקונים והברורים הנפלאים, הנעשים עד עתה על ידי מיתת עשרה הרוגי מלכות, כמובא בכתבים. ובאמת מיתת כל הצדיקים היא בחינת מסירת נפש על קדוש השם, בפרט מיתת הצדיקים שבחוץ לארץ, שהכל הוא כענין התפלה בבחינת דין, שמוסרים גופם שיהיה נקבר בחוץ לארץ, ששם שליטת הסטרא אחרא, ונדמה להסטרא אחרא שהיא בולעת את הגוף הקדוש הזה, אבל זה הגוף הקדוש הוא בעל כח גדול ועומד להסטרא אחרא בצוארה, עד שמוכרחת על ידי זה להקיא הקאות הרבה מקרבה ומבטנה, עד שיגמר הצדיק מה שהתחיל, כי גם בחייו עסק כל ימיו בזה ומסר נפשו בשביל זה, אך אחר הסתלקותו, אז אינו פוסק מלעסק בעבודה הקדושה הזאת, עד שיגמר הכל לטובה כרצונו. ועל כן שם, על קברו הקדוש, יכול כל אחד להתתקן, אפלו הגרוע שבגרועים, אם יזכה לבוא לשם בחייו ויבקש ויתפלל שם על תקון נפשו, וזה גם ענין העשרה קפיטל תהלים שנתיסדו לומר שם, עין פנים. (הלכות חל המועד, הלכה ד', אות יד טו):
segments.en:
13.
The great virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for there everyone can be repaired. Even one who is between the teeth of the adversary, G-d forbid — the great Tzadik can extract him from there — when one comes to his holy grave and wishes to return in complete teshuvah. For the death of the great Tzadik is very high and elevated and exalted. And then specifically he intensifies with all his strength to complete what he needs to complete for the benefit of the souls of Israel. For the death of the Tzadik is the aspect of prayer in the aspect of judgment — for the great ba'al ko'ach [master of power] prays — and the sitra achra swallows it. And the prayer — since it is very holy and came from a great ba'al ko'ach — the sitra achra does not have the power to swallow it entirely. Rather, on the contrary — the prayer stands in its throat [b'tzavoroh] — until the sitra achra is compelled through this to vomit and expel and return all the holinesses it has swallowed — including the very essence of its vitality.

And this is the secret of the wondrous repairs and refinements being performed to this day through the death of the ten martyrs [asarah harugei malchus] — as is brought in the sacred writings. And in truth the death of all the Tzaddikim is the aspect of mesiras nefesh [self-sacrifice] for the sanctification of G-d's Name. Especially the death of the Tzaddikim in the diaspora — where all of this is in the manner of the prayer in the aspect of judgment. For they surrender their body to be buried in the diaspora — where the dominion of the sitra achra resides. And it seems to the sitra achra that it is swallowing this holy body. But this holy body is a great ba'al ko'ach and stands in the sitra achra's throat — until it is compelled through this to vomit greatly from within itself and from its belly — until the Tzadik completes what he began. For even during his lifetime he engaged in this all his days and gave his soul for this. But after his passing, he does not stop engaging in this holy service — until he completes everything for the good as he wishes.

And therefore there — upon his holy grave — every person can be repaired. Even the worst of the worst. If he merits to come there during his lifetime and to request and pray there for the repair of his soul. And this too is the matter of the ten Psalms chapters ordained to be said there — see inside.

(Hilchos Chol HaMo'ed, Halacha 4, items 14–15).

requiredNotes.text: שני here is שִׁנֵּי, “the teeth of,” not שְׁנֵי, “two.” The complete cited Chol HaMo’ed 4:14 in the local source has בין שיני הס"ם; the independently numbered pointed digital text has בֵּין שִׁנֵּי הַס"ם. Items 14–15 develop the same swallowing, throat and disgorging image. The English therefore reads “between the teeth of the adversary”; the compiler’s Hebrew and abbreviation are unchanged.

The passage’s assurances retain their conditions: coming to the holy grave and wishing to return in complete repentance; its closing assurance speaks of coming during one’s lifetime and requesting and praying for the soul’s repair. The text refers to ten Psalm chapters without listing their numbers. The closing citation to Chol HaMo’ed 4:14–15 has been checked against both complete local paragraphs and the independently numbered digital witness.

anchors.text: אם יזכה לבוא לשם בחייו ויבקש ויתפלל שם על תקון נפשו
wishes to return in complete teshuvah

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore they are four cups — corresponding to the four expressions of redemption. For the essential redemption depends on faith as above. And the four cups correspond to the four aspects — which are: faith, and prayer, and miracles, and the Land of Israel. Each cup corresponding to one aspect individually, as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he:
יד.
על ידי שזוכין לפרנס את הצדיק, על ידי זה בנקל יותר לקבל ממנו הארת דעתו הקדושה, עד שיכולין לזכות על ידי זה לאכל בעצמו גם כן בקדושה גדולה ולקבל הארת הרצון בשעת האכילה. גם על ידי זה על ידי זה יוכל לקבל הארה יתרה מהשארת הדעת, שנשאר מהצדיק גם אחר הסתלקותו. (הלכות פדיון בכור, הלכה ה', אות ז, י):
segments.en:
14.
Through meriting to support the Tzadik [financially] — through this it is easier to receive from him the illumination of his holy da'as. Until one can merit through this to eat himself also in great holiness and to receive the illumination of will at the time of eating. Also through this — [through this] — one can receive extra illumination from the remaining da'as [hashoras hada'as] left by the Tzadik — even after his passing.

(Hilchos Pidyon Bechor, Halacha 5, items 7, 10).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: In every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt. For this aspect is in every person and at every time. For the essential bitterness of the exile for every person is the aspect of the entanglement of money and livelihood. And the essential redemption of the soul for every person is commensurate with how much he merits to draw close to the truly righteous Tzaddikim — through which he breaks the desire for money and merits to be happy with his portion. Through feeling his poverty in all aspects: body and soul and money. And through this he merits the aspect of redemption — the aspect of holy wealth. Until through this he can merit even actual great physical wealth. And this is the essential complete redemption that will come through our righteous Mashiach — when all wealth will be returned to holiness for Israel. For they will all be Tzaddikim then. And as is explained in many verses — the great wealth that will be then. And all this will be merited specifically through the bitter poverty they endured in this exile. And even then — when they emerge from this exile and merit wealth — even so they will not forget their poverty and will not become arrogant. Rather, they will consider themselves poor — as it is written: "And a poor and lowly people will take refuge in Him" [Zephaniah 3:12]. And also Mashiach himself is called ani [poor] and "riding upon a donkey" [Zechariah 9:9]. For the essential true wealth — spiritually and physically — is merited through true poverty and lowliness as above.

segments.he:
טו.
גם יכולין לקבל על ידי זה שפע ברכה ועשירות גדול (שם):
segments.en:
15.
Also one can receive through this [supporting the Tzadik] an abundant flow of blessing and great wealth.

(ibid.).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One who wishes to enter the service of G-d — this is truly the aspect of the exodus from Egypt. For the essential exodus from Egypt is going out from impurity to purity — from the impurity and defilement of Pharaoh and Egypt to the holiness of Israel. As it is written: "When you bring forth the people from Egypt, you shall serve G-d, etc." [Exodus 3:12]. And this is necessarily what passes over a person at every time and in every generation — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "In every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt." For all that passed over Israel at the exodus from Egypt, and the receiving of the Torah, and thereafter — and all the wars to conquer the Land of Israel — and all that passed over us afterwards — all of it, precisely and exactly, passes over every person who wishes to merit the life of eternity. For necessarily, many kinds of countless battles will pass over him. And every time he wishes to awaken and strengthen himself in the service of G-d — they intensify each time more, especially in the beginning. Which is the aspect of: "Let the work be heavier upon the men, etc." — said at the beginning of the redemption from Egypt. For when the sitra achra sees that a true Tzadik — in the aspect of Moshe — comes and wishes to bring the person of Israel out from the exile of his soul — it provokes and intensifies against him more and more, and makes this world and the desires and the livelihood heavier upon him — until it is difficult for him to move from his place to return to G-d.

segments.he:
טז.
על ידי ההליכה והנסיעה, שכל אחד הולך ונוסע ממקומו להצדיק, על ידי זה מעלה מקומו לבחינת מקומו של עולם, שהוא הצדיק. וזה בחינת מה שנוסעין והולכין על קברי צדיקים, בפרט קדם ראש השנה, כי במקום ששוכב הצדיק, שם מקום מנוחתו, בבחינת: יבא שלום ינוחו על משכבותם, ועקר מנוחת הצדיק הוא כשמקושר ונכלל בבחינת כסא הכבוד, בחינת מקומו של עולם, ששם עקר המנוחה והנחלה בבחינת: וכסא כבוד ינחילם וכו', ועל כן שם, במקום גניזת הצדיק, זוכה כל אחד שירחמו עליו מלמעלה וידונו אותו לכף זכות על ידי בחינת מקומו של עולם. (הלכות שלוחין, הלכה ד', אות יג):
segments.en:
16.
Through the journey and travel that each person makes from his place to the Tzadik — through this he elevates his place to the aspect of mekomo shel olam [the place of the world] — which is the Tzadik. And this is the aspect of what people journey and travel to the graves of the Tzaddikim — especially before Rosh Hashanah. For in the place where the Tzadik lies — that is the place of his rest — in the aspect of: "he will come to peace; they will rest upon their resting places". And the essential rest of the Tzadik is when he is bound and encompassed in the aspect of the Throne of Glory — the aspect of mekomo shel olam — where the essential rest and the inheritance reside — in the aspect of: "And a glorious throne shall He cause them to inherit, etc.". And therefore there — in the place of the Tzadik's resting — every person merits that he will be judged mercifully from Above — and be judged to the scale of merit — through the aspect of mekomo shel olam.

(Hilchos Shlichin, Halacha 4, item 13).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: But the way of Israel the holy people — who hold the craft of their ancestors in their hands — is that every time they cry out to G-d. And through this they subdue each time Pharaoh and his forces — which are the sitra achra and its sects. But even though they subdue them — even so, they return and intensify every single time. And so, time after time, many times — as we saw with Pharaoh: that every time some plague came upon him he yielded somewhat, and afterwards he hardened his heart and returned and intensified. And even after the entire exodus from Egypt was complete, he returned and gathered his forces and pursued after them and caught up with them at the sea. And then Israel was in great distress and in great straits — as our Sages of blessed memory said on the verse: "My dove in the clefts of the rock, etc." [Song of Songs 2:14]. And likewise precisely so it passes over every person at every time, each according to his level.

segments.he:
יז.
בכל פעם שבוכין על הסתלקות הצדיק ומחפשין ומבקשין אותו כראוי, אזי מוציאין קדושתו על ידי הבן או התלמיד, שממלא מקום אביו ורבו, כי זה כלל גדול, שאין הצדיק מסתלק מן העולם עד שנולד אחר תחתיו, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: וזרח השמש ובא השמש וכו', אבל צריכין לבקש ולחפש אחר זה הרבה הרבה, בפרט בדורות הללו, ועל כן אף על פי שצריכין לבכות ולספד הרבה על הסתלקות הצדיק, אבל צריכין לזהר מאד, שלא להכשל על ידי זה לומר, שכבר מת הצדיק ואפס תקוה, חס ושלום, ולא נשאר בעולם חליפתו והשארתו, כי זה פגם עצום, מאד כי בודאי הצדיק לא מת, ובודאי נשאר השארת קדושתו אצל בניו ותלמידיו, רק שצריכין לחפש ולבקש אחר זה מאד מאד, ועל ידי כל חפוש ובקשה מוצאין בודאי קדושת השארתו אצל בניו ותלמידיו, שזהו בחינת: שם מת אהרן ויכהן אלעזר בנו תחתיו, כמבאר בפנים. (שם הלכה ה', אות יז):
segments.en:
17.
Every time one weeps over the passing of the Tzadik and searches and seeks after him as is proper — then one draws out his holiness through the son or the disciple who fills the place of his father and master. For this is a great principle: the Tzadik does not depart from the world until another is born in his place. As our Sages of blessed memory said [on the verse]: "The sun also rises and the sun also sets, etc.". But one must seek and search after this very much — [very much] — especially in these generations.

And therefore even though one must weep and mourn greatly over the passing of the Tzadik — even so, one must be very careful not to stumble through this and say that the Tzadik has already died and there is no more hope, G-d forbid, and that no successor or remnant of him remains in the world. For this is a very great blemish. For certainly the Tzadik has not died — and certainly the remnant [hashoras] of his holiness remains with his sons and his disciples. Only one must search and seek after this very — [very] — greatly. And through every search and seeking, one certainly finds the holiness of his remnant with his sons and disciples. Which is the aspect of: "There Aaron died, and Elazar his son served as priest in his place" — as explained in the inner teachings.

(ibid., Halacha 5, item 17).
