history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of the kriyas Yam Suf [splitting of the Red Sea] — the aspect of: "And the Children of Israel came within the sea upon dry land" [Exodus 14:22]. That is: when the insolent waters — which are the aspect of evil thoughts, etc., which are called literally the depths of the sea — intensify, G-d forbid, and there is nowhere to flee — neither forward nor backward nor to any side. Exactly as was the case then at the splitting of the Sea — the sea was storming before them, the Egyptians were behind them, and on their sides were wild beasts and serpents and scorpions. When then the soul of the person of Israel is in great distress and great straits — then there is no remedy except to cry out to G-d. And then G-d sends him a great strengthening in his heart and his mind — not to look behind him at all at the confusing thoughts, which are the aspect of the depths of the sea aforementioned. Rather, he should rush like a warrior to run the path — to pass through all the thoughts and confusions, etc. — and to walk in the holy path upon which he is engaged: in Torah and prayer, etc.

segments.he:
יח.
דרך כמה אנשים, שאומרים אחר הסתלקות הצדיק, חס ושלום, שעתה כבר לא נשאר לנו כלום, חס ושלום ואף על פי שמצד אחד אומרים קצת אמת, כי בודאי לא נשאר ממש צדיק כזה, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: פני משה כפני חמה, פני יהושוע כפני לבנה, אוי לאותה בושה וכו' אבל אוף על פי כן אסור לשאר, חס ושלום, בזה לומר, שמחמת זה אפס תקוה, חס ושלום, כי נהפוך הוא, כי לא יטש השם את עמו לעולם וממשלתך בכל דור ודור, על כן צריכין להאמין, שאף על פי שצריכין בודאי להתגעגע מאד אחרי הצדיק האמת בחינת משה, אוף על פי כן צריכין לסים בדברי נחמה לנחם ולשמח עצמו בהשארתו, דהינו חדושי התורה הקדושה, שנשאר ממנו על ידי ספריו ותלמידיו, כי מהצדיק האמתי בודאי נשאר השארה טובה לנצח, רק צריכין לבקש ולחפש הרבה כנ"ל. (שם, אות יח):
segments.en:
18.
It is the way of many people to say after the passing of the Tzadik, G-d forbid: "Now we have nothing left at all, G-d forbid." And even though from one side they speak some truth — for certainly there has not remained literally a Tzadik exactly like him. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "The face of Moshe is like the face of the sun; the face of Yehoshua is like the face of the moon. Woe for that shame, etc." — even so, it is forbidden to remain, G-d forbid, with this and to say that therefore all hope is lost, G-d forbid. For the opposite is the case — for G-d will never abandon His people. And "Your dominion is in every generation". Therefore one must believe that even though one must certainly pine very greatly after the true Tzadik in the aspect of Moshe — even so, one must conclude with words of comfort — to comfort and gladden oneself in his remnant: that is, the holy innovations of Torah that remain from him through his books and his disciples. For from a truly righteous Tzadik, certainly a good remnant remains forever. Only one must search and seek much as above.

(ibid., item 18).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of: "Speak to the Children of Israel and let them journey forth" [Exodus 14:15] — that they should go their way and leap into the sea — and not think and not look behind them at all. And so they did — they entered into the sea up to their nostrils, as our Sages of blessed memory said. That is, they did not look at all at the insolent rushing waters — rather, they walked in confidence upon their way and engaged in their service in Torah and prayer within the intensification of the roaring crashing waves, which are the thoughts and the confusions. And they did not look behind them at all — rather, they did what they had to do. And then — when G-d saw the firmness of their heart, that they did not abandon their service through any confusion in the world, even though they had already entered the water up to their nostrils — then G-d had compassion upon them and split the sea before them. "And the Children of Israel came within the sea upon dry land." For so it is: when one strengthens oneself with great strengthening to go in one's way in prayer and service — and not to look behind at all — then suddenly they are nullified by themselves entirely, exactly like the sea that was nullified before Israel and turned into dry land.

segments.he: ערך צדקה
segments.en: Tzedakah

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: In the matter of Pesach Sheini [the second Passover] — it is alluded to that there is no despair in the world whatsoever. For even one who is impure or is on a very far road [derech rechokah] from G-d — and is unable to bring the offering of G-d at its appointed time — that is, does not merit to always serve His service in proper order, at its time and season, as is fitting for a person of Israel — even so, if he does not despair of himself because of this and goes to the true Tzadik — who is in the aspect of Moshe — to seek G-d. And asks and requests: "Why should we be diminished from not bringing the offering of G-d, etc.?" [Numbers 9:7]. For even though I have defiled my soul and been distanced from G-d — even so, I ask for counsel and a means as to how to draw close to G-d at least from now on. For certainly there is a counsel for me too as to how to draw close to G-d. Then G-d has compassion upon him — and he merits through this the ultimate elevation. And merits through this to add a Torah portion [parshah b'Torah]. For through seeking and searching for "where is the place of His glory?" — through this one merits the subsequent revelation of the Torah — [of the Torah] — as explained elsewhere.

segments.he:
א.
בודאי השם יתברך יכול לפרנס העניים ולתן להם כל טוב בעצמו, אך עקר מצות הצדקה היא מחמת שהממון כבר ביד העשיר, ובידו לעשות בו כרצונו, והוא מתגבר בבחירתו ונותן מכיסו לצדקה, זה יקר מאד אצל השם יתברך, כי על ידי זה ממשיך חסדים בעולם, וזהו רצונו יתברך, שבן אדם הבעל בחירה ימשיך לעולם על ידי הצדקה, שנותן להעני בבחירתו, ובכל זה רואין גדל כח הבחירה. (הלכות ברכות השחר, הלכה ה', אות צא):
segments.en:
1.
Certainly G-d, blessed be He, can sustain the poor and give them all good directly. But the essential commandment of tzedakah is because the money is already in the wealthy person's hand — and it is in his power to do with it as he wishes. And he overpowers [his inclination] through his free will and gives from his own pocket to tzedakah. This is very precious before G-d, blessed be He. For through this he draws chassadim [kindnesses] into the world. And this is His blessed will — that the human being who has free will draw [kindnesses] into the world through the tzedakah he gives to the poor of his own free will. And in all of this we see the greatness of the power of free will.

(Hilchos Bircas HaShachar, Halacha 5, item 91).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Even though in truth one must hurry and hasten very — [very] — greatly to rescue one's soul. And especially one who has already stumbled and been caught in what he has been caught, G-d protect us — even so, it is — [it is] — impossible to press the moment. And one must wait and wait — until G-d looks down from Heaven and sees. But even so, even within the time of the waiting and the delay — it is forbidden to remove one's mind from this. Rather, one must hope and anticipate and look forward and count and tell the days — and long and yearn at every time: when will he merit the day of the complete salvation of his soul?

segments.he:
ב.
התקון של כל הולכי דרכים בגשמיות ורוחניות הוא על ידי צדקה, כי עקר ידיעת הדרך הישר באמת לאמתו אי אפשר להורות בפרוש, כי אם ברמז בבחינת: אשכילך ואורך בדרך זו תלך איעצה עליך עיני, כי אי אפשר לבאר כל המבוכות והטעויות שיש בהליכת הדרכים, אפלו בגשמיות, מכל שכן בענין דרכים ונתיבות ברוחניות בעבודת השם, שבודאי אי אפשר לבאר ולפרש לכל אחד ואחד הדרך הישר בכל יום ובכל עת להיכן יפנה להציל נפשו ממה שצריך להנצל, כי אם ברמז, שמרמזין לאדם בכל עת בדרך זו ילך; וכל זה נתתקן על ידי צדקה בחינת: צדקת תמים תישר דרכו, כי על ידי צדקה זוכין לילך בדרך הישר בגשמיות ורוחניות. (הלכות ברכות הודאה, הלכה ה', אות ה):
segments.en:
2.
The repair of all wayfarers — physically and spiritually — is through tzedakah. For the essential knowledge of the truly straight path in its true truth — it is impossible to instruct explicitly, but only through a hint — in the aspect of: "I will instruct you and show you the way you should go — I will counsel you with My eye upon you". For it is impossible to explain all the confusions and errors that arise in traveling the paths — even in the physical. How much more so in the matter of spiritual paths and trails in the service of G-d — where it is certainly impossible to explain and specify for each and every person the straight path at every day and every time, as to where to turn to rescue his soul from what he needs to be rescued from — except through a hint. That a hint is given to a person at every time: "in this way go." And all of this is repaired through tzedakah — in the aspect of: "the righteousness of the wholesome straightens his way". For through tzedakah one merits to walk in the straight path — physically and spiritually.

(Hilchos Bircas HaHodaah, Halacha 5, item 5).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of the Sefirah [Counting of the Omer] — where we do nothing except count the days and the weeks. And through this we draw upon ourselves the holiness of the renewed receiving of the Torah each year. That is, through this very aspect aforementioned — that we want and desire and yearn to receive the Torah. And according to the strength of our will and our strong yearning — certainly we would want to receive it with alacrity immediately and at once. But in truth it is impossible to press the moment — and it is necessary to wait until — [until] — the fiftieth day. But even so, even now it is forbidden to forget and to remove one's mind from this, G-d forbid. Which is the aspect of why we count the days — for the counting shows the very — [very] — essence of the longing and the pining — [and the pining]. Like one who yearns and craves for some matter — then the way is to count the days until he attains his longing. Likewise, we count and reckon the days and the weeks — which shows the essence of the longing and the strong will we have for the receiving of the Torah.

segments.he:
ג.
מעלת מצות הצדקה הוא בלי שעור, וכל התורה וכל תקון העולמות תלוי בזה, כי הכל נברא בשביל כבודו, וכל כבודו נתגלה על ידי הצדקה, שעל ידה נעשה כלי לקבל השפעת הנעם העליון, שעל ידי זה נעשה הולדה ונתגלה כבודו, כמבאר בפנים, ועל כן שקולה צדקה ככל התורה כולה, כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה. אבל צריכין להרבות בצדקה מאד ולבקש מהשם יתברך, שיזכה לקים מצות הצדקה כראוי, שיתן הצדקה בלב שלם למען שמו יתברך באמת ושיזמין לו השם יתברך עניים הגונים לזכות בהם, כי עקר תקון הצדקה - שיתגדל כבודו יתברך על ידי זה כנ"ל, על כן צריך לכון בצדקתו רק בשביל כבוד השם יתברך, לא בשביל כבוד עצמו, חס ושלום לא כמצוי בכמה אנשים, שנותנים צדקה רק למי שיש להם ממשלה וכבוד בעולם, ועל כן הצדקה גם להם לכבוד, ועל עניים הגונים וכשרים העוסקים בתורה ועבודת השם באמת אינם משגיחים כלל ומעלימין עיניהם מהם נמצא, שהצדקה שנותנים הוא רק בשביל כבוד עצמן. ואף על פי שבודאי גם בזאת הצדקה יש נקודות טובות, אבל על ידי צדקה כזאת אין נעשה הכלי הנ"ל בשלמות לקבל על ידה שפע נעם העליון בשלמות, ועל כן עקר תקון הצדקה - שתהיה בבחינת מנחה, שהיא קרבן עני, שנתינתו מועטת, ועל כן אינו מתפאר בה, רק כונתו בקרבנו רק לשמים לבד, כמו כן העשיר - אף על פי שנותן הרבה לצדקה, חלילה לו להתגאות בחינת הצדקה ולהתכון בה לכבוד עצמו, רק אף על פי שיתן לצדקה הון רב, אוף על פי כן יהיה בעיניו כעני, כי באמת נגדו יתברך הכל עניים, כמו שכתוב: מי הקדימני ואשלם, כי הכל רק ממנו יתברך, כמו שכתוב: ממך הכל ומידך נתנו לך, ועל כן דוד המלך עליו השלום, בעת שנתן הון רב לנדבת בית המקדש אמר: 
והנה בעניי הכינותי וכו', כי החזיק כל נתינתו לעניות, וצדקה כזאת יקרה מאד, כי הוא בחינת מנחת עני, שחביבה מאד מחמת שכונתו רק לשמים בלי שום התפארות עצמו כלל, ועל כן נקראת צדקה כזאת בשם מנחה בחינת: מגישי מנחה בצדקה. (הלכות תפלת המנחה, הלכה ו', אות ד):
segments.en:
3.
The virtue of the commandment of tzedakah is without measure — and all the Torah and all the repair of the worlds depends upon this. For everything was created for His honor — and all His honor is revealed through tzedakah. Through which a vessel is made to receive the flow of the supernal delight [no'am ha'elyon] — through which birth [holadah] occurs and His honor is revealed. As explained within [the cited work]. And therefore tzedakah is equivalent to the entire Torah — as our Sages of blessed memory said.

But one must give much tzedakah — and request from G-d, blessed be He, that he merit to fulfill the commandment of tzedakah as is proper: that he give the tzedakah with a full heart for the sake of His blessed Name, truly. And that G-d, blessed be He, send him worthy poor people through whom to merit. For the essential repair of tzedakah is that through it His honor (blessed be He) should be magnified as above. And therefore one must intend in his charity only for the honor of G-d, blessed be He — not for his own honor, G-d forbid. Not as is found with many people who give tzedakah only to those who have dominion and prestige in the world — and therefore the tzedakah is also for their honor. And upon the worthy and upright poor who engage in Torah and the service of G-d in truth — they pay no attention to them at all and avert their eyes from them. It is thus found that the tzedakah they give is only for their own honor.

And even though certainly even in such tzedakah there are good points — but through tzedakah such as this, the aforementioned vessel is not made in perfection to receive through it the flow of the supernal delight in perfection. And therefore the essential repair of tzedakah is that it should be in the aspect of a minchah [meal-offering] — which is the sacrifice of the poor person, whose giving is small. And therefore he does not take pride in it — rather, his intention in his offering is only toward Heaven alone. Likewise the wealthy person — even though he gives much to tzedakah — far be it from him to be boastful in the aspect of tzedakah and to intend in it for his own honor. Rather, even though he gives much to tzedakah — even so, in his own eyes he should be like a poor person. For in truth before Him, blessed be He, all are poor — as it is written: "Who can precede Me and I will pay him?". For everything is only from Him, blessed be He. As it is written: "For everything is from You and from Your hand we have given You". And therefore King David, peace be upon him, at the time he gave much wealth for the donation toward the Temple said: "And now I have prepared with my poverty, etc." — for he considered all his giving as poverty. And such tzedakah is very precious — for it is the aspect of the minchas ani [offering of the poor] — which is very beloved because his intention is only toward Heaven with no self-glorification whatsoever. And therefore such tzedakah is called by the name minchah — in the aspect of: "those who offer a minchah in righteousness".

(Hilchos Tefillas HaMinchah, Halacha 6, item 4).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore in truth all of Israel is accustomed to fulfill the commandment of counting the Omer with great awakening and great yearning toward G-d. And through this we merit to draw in perfection the aspect of hot words like coals of fire — in the aspect of: "For love is as strong as death, etc." [Song of Songs 8:6]. That is, through the greatness of the holy love and yearning aforementioned — one merits: "its flashes are flashes of fire" [Song of Songs 8:6]. And through this one merits the receiving of the Torah in the aspect of: "And you heard His words from within the fire" [Deuteronomy 4:36] — as mentioned above.

segments.he:
ד.
ביותר צריכין לתן צדקה ברגלים כדי להכניע מצח הנחש ולגלות מצח הרצון, שעל ידי זה נזכה לשמע קול הקריאה של יום טוב, שקורא ומגלה את הרצון, שעל ידי זה זוכין לשמחת יום טוב. וזה שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה ענין יום טוב: אם אתה משמח את שלי, אני משמח את שלך, כי על ידי זה זוכין לשמחת יום טוב. (הלכות סימני דגים, הלכה ג', אות ו):
segments.en:
4.
One must give more tzedakah on the Festivals — in order to subdue the forehead [metzach] of the serpent and to reveal the forehead of will [metzach haratzon]. Through which one merits to hear the voice of the herald of Yom Tov — which calls out and reveals the will. Through which one merits the joy of Yom Tov. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said regarding Yom Tov: "If you gladden Mine — I will gladden yours." For through this one merits the joy of Yom Tov.

(Hilchos Simanai Dogim, Halacha 3, item 6).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: All the days of the year one must prepare himself for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For the essential thing is Rosh Hashanah. For just as a person must prepare himself all the days of his life for the great and awesome Day of Judgment in the future — likewise in the particular, he must prepare himself all the days of the year for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For it is awesome and dreadful, etc. And especially one must begin and prepare himself when he sees the days approaching — which is from the fifteenth of Av onwards. For then begins the sweetening of the sin of the Golden Calf and the sin of the Spies — through which, in all of this, the holy memory [zikaron d'kedushah] was blemished. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "From the day the Tablets were broken, forgetting descended upon the world." And on the fifteenth of Av began the sweetening of the breaking of the Tablets — and the illumination of the forty days of favor begins to shine. For then they subsequently received on Yom Kippur the second Tablets — which merited the aspect of the repair of memory. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said: "No days were as good for Israel as the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur." For on the fifteenth of Av begins to shine the illumination from the second Tablets given on Yom Kippur. And therefore on the fifteenth of Av the sin of the Spies was also repaired — for on it the desert generation ceased dying, as our Sages of blessed memory said. And therefore from the fifteenth of Av one must begin to rise at midnight — which is the aspect of the repair of memory.

segments.he:
ה.
על ידי צדקה משככין חמימות הלב הבוער לתאות משגל ולתאות ממון, אשר שניהם תלויים זה בזה, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות קדושין, הלכה ג', אות ב, ה):
segments.en:
5.
Through tzedakah one appeases the burning heat of the heart that blazes toward the desire for sexual union and the desire for money — both of which depend upon one another, as explained in the inner teachings.

(Hilchos Kidushin, Halacha 3, items 2, 5).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And afterwards during the month of Elul one engages in this more and more. And all of Israel is awakened then and remembers G-d and the World to Come. And this is the aspect of the blowing of the shofar throughout the month of Elul. For the shofar is the aspect of remembrance — as it is written: "And it shall be for you a remembrance" [Numbers 10:10]. And the essential repair of memory flows on Rosh Hashanah — when the essential commandment of the shofar is performed. Which is the Day of Remembrance [yom hazikaron]. For it is the first of the Ten Days of Repentance — and one must draw upon himself the aforementioned remembrance. Through which comes the essential teshuvah. And for this purpose one must journey to the Tzaddikim for Rosh Hashanah. For this is the essential occupation of the Tzaddikim always — to remind us of our eternal purpose in the World to Come, and to teach us counsels and straight paths to merit this. And especially the Tzaddikim engage in this on Rosh Hashanah, as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he: ערך ציצית
segments.en: Tzitzis

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this remembrance is in the general and in the particular. And this is the secret of the year [shanah] and the awakening of the year [his'orrus hashanah] at Rosh Hashanah. For the shanah is the aspect of remembrance of the World to Come in the general — for then the soul ascends to the aspect of the World to Come. And afterwards — in the awakening of the year — then one must engage in this in the particular. And afterwards — on Yom Kippur — then comes the completion of the repair of the remembrance. And therefore the second Tablets were given then. And the High Priest entered on it into the innermost chamber, as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he:
א.
כל אחד מישראל - בפנימיות נפשו הוא משתוקק ובוער מאד להשם יתברך, מחמת שבפנימיות הוא מסתכל בכל עת אל התכלית, שהוא אור האין סוף, שמשם שרשו, ורוצה להתדבק ולהכלל שם, אך מחמת שבחינה זאת היא בבחינת רצוא ושוב, וכשהוא בבחינת ושוב, אז אין הכלים של המחין, שהם בחינת לבושין, יכולין לקבל אור הזריחה משם, ואז על פי רב נשכח ממנו אור הרשימה של הבטול לגמרי, ועל ידי מצות ציצית מתקנין הלבושים, שהם בחינת בחינת הכלים של המחין, כדי שיוכלו לקבל אור הזריחה של הרשימה מהבטול, שמשם שרש כל התורה, וזה בחינת: וראיתם אותו וכו': שעקרו נאמר על התכלת שבציצית, הינו שצריכין לראות ולהסתכל מאד על התכלית, שהוא בחינת תכלת, כמבאר בפנים. וזה: ולא תתורו אחרי לבבכם ואחרי עיניכם, שיסתם עיניו מחיזו דהאי עלמא לגמרי ויכון ראיתו והסתלקותו רק התכלית לבד - למען תזכרו ועשיתם את כל מצותי, כי על ידי מצות ציצית זוכין לזכר היטב את אור הרשימה הנ"ל, שמשם נמשך כלל התורה ומצוות. (הלכות נטילת ידים שחרית, הלכה ד', אות ח):
segments.en:
1.
Every single person of Israel — in the inner depth of his soul — yearns and burns very greatly for G-d, blessed be He. Because in the inner depth he gazes at all times toward the purpose [tachlis] — which is the light of the Infinite [ohr ha'ain sof] — from which his root derives. And he wishes to cleave and be encompassed there. But since this aspect is in the aspect of ratzo v'shov [advance and retreat] — and when he is in the aspect of shov [retreat], then the vessels of the expanded consciousness [kailim d'hamoi'ach] — which are the aspect of the garments — are unable to receive the light of the shining from there. And then most often the light of the impression [reshimah] of the nullification [bitul] is entirely forgotten by him. And through the commandment of tzitzis — the garments are repaired. Which are the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the vessels of the expanded consciousness. So that they can receive the light of the shining of the impression from the nullification — from which is the root of all Torah. And this is the aspect of: "And you shall see it, etc." — whose essential [reference] is to the techeiles [blue dye] in the tzitzis. That is, one must look and gaze greatly upon the purpose [tachlis] — which is the aspect of techeiles — as explained in the inner teachings. And this: "and you shall not go astray after your hearts and after your eyes" — that he should close his eyes from the sight of this world entirely and direct his vision and his gaze only toward the ultimate purpose alone. "So that you shall remember and do all My commandments". For through the commandment of tzitzis one merits to well remember the light of the impression aforementioned — from which flows the totality of Torah and commandments.

(Hilchos Netilas Yodayim Shacharis, Halacha 4, item 8).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

requiredNotes.text: The supplied compiler text has והסתלקותו, literally “his withdrawal.” Its cited source, הלכות נטילת ידים שחרית ד:ח, reads והסתכלותו, “his gazing,” in the instruction to direct one’s sight toward the ultimate purpose. The English follows that corroborated sense; the compiler’s Hebrew remains unchanged.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And afterwards one enters the sukkah — which is the encompassing clouds of glory [ananei kavod] that protect us so that the evil eye no longer has dominion over us — which is the aspect of the husk of Amalek. So as not to blemish again, G-d forbid, the holy memory we drew upon ourselves in these days — especially on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. And this is the aspect of the joy one multiplies on Sukkos — in order to repair also through this the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the imagination [hamedameh]. For all of this is the aspect of the repair of memory aforementioned. And therefore one then takes the four species of the lulav. And the holy Zohar explains that through this we take Him, blessed be He, as it were, in our hands — that is, we draw upon ourselves the remembrance in the particular: which is the aspect of the hints whereby G-d contracts Himself from the Infinite to the infinite [me'ain sof ad ain techlis] in thought, speech, and action each day — and hints to the person everywhere and at all times to draw close to Him. Which is the aspect of the wavings that are waved to all directions. That is, we draw upon ourselves these hints aforementioned.

segments.he:
ב.
ציצית הוא שמירה גדולה מהקלפות והסטרא אחרא, מחמת ששם נקשר אור הרשימה הקדושה הנ"ל. (שם, אות יד):
segments.en:
2.
Tzitzis is a great protection from the kelipos [husks] and the sitra achra — because within them is bound the light of the aforementioned holy impression.

(ibid., item 14).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One must journey to the truly righteous Tzaddikim for Rosh Hashanah. For only they can draw the paths of teshuvah in perfection. And the essential [need] is to sweeten the force of the judgment of Rosh Hashanah and to draw joy upon oneself — through which comes the essential repair of teshuvah. For even though the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is the aspect of a broken heart — for the penitent must have a broken heart. Which is the aspect of: "If the shofar is blown in the city, will the people not tremble?" [Amos 3:6]. But after the broken heart one must come to joy. And this is the aspect of: "Fortunate is the people who know the teruah, etc." [Psalms 89:16]. And adjacent to it: "In Your name they will rejoice all the day, etc." [Psalms 89:17].

segments.he:
ג.
ציצית הם בחינת תקון הברית, תקון הכללי, כי על ידם מרים המחין וממשיך לבנונית לתקן הפגמים של כל החטאים, רחמנא לצלן, ועל ידי זה נתתקנין הבגדים ונעשין בבחינת בגדים לבנים, ועל כן יש בהם ט"ל כריכות - נגד הטל אורות, שזוכין על ידי שמירת הברית ושתים עשרה אצבעות ארכן - נגד שנים עשר שבטים, שנכלל נשמתו בהם על ידי תקון הכללי, ועל ידי זה זוכין לדבר דבורים המתקבלים ונשמעים, ועל כן עקר תקון התפלה, שתהא מקובלת, היא בעטיפת טלית של ציצית. (הלכות ציצית, הלכה א'):
segments.en:
3.
Tzitzis is the aspect of the repair of the bris — the tikun hakelali [general repair]. For through them the expanded consciousness is elevated and whiteness is drawn to repair the blemishes of all sins, G-d protect us. And through this the garments are repaired and made into the aspect of white garments. And therefore they have thirty-nine [ט"ל] windings — corresponding to the dew of lights [tal orosin] — which one merits through the guarding of the bris. And twelve finger-breadths in length — corresponding to the twelve tribes — in whom his soul is encompassed through the tikun hakelali. And through this one merits to speak words that are accepted and heard. And therefore the essential repair of prayer — that it be accepted — is through the wrapping of the tallis of tzitzis.

(Hilchos Tzitzis, Halacha 1).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The essential holiness of a person is when he confines himself within his home and his chamber — in the aspect of: "Go, my people, enter your chambers, etc." [Isaiah 26:20]. And it is said: "Walk humbly with your G-d" [Micah 6:8]. And this is the aspect of the praise said of Torah scholars: "All the glory of the king's daughter is within" [Psalms 45:14]. For the essential splendor and holiness of a person is when he sits within his home — where the essential flow of holiness resides. But outside is the domain of the dominion of the outer forces.

segments.he: ערך רצון
segments.en: Will

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore it would have been fitting that a person always sit within his home. But a person is necessarily compelled to go outside as well every single time. And this is the aspect of ail v'nafak [entering and exiting]. For even though it would have been fitting for a person to always be attached to holiness in the aspect of entry — even so, the essential perfection of holiness is specifically when a person merits to be ail v'nafak. For a person necessarily passes through many ascents and descents every single day. And when he merits to be expert in the halacha [baki b'halacha] — in the aspect of baki b'ail, baki b'nafak [expert in entering, expert in exiting] — to fulfill as it is written: "If I ascend to the heavens — there You are, and if I make my bed in the abyss — behold You are there" [Psalms 139:8] — to hold fast to G-d always with a strong bond, both in ascent and in descent — then he merits to elevate even external places and lower levels all to holiness. And then the descent is the ultimate purpose of the ascent.

segments.he:
א.
בכל מה שעובר על האדם, איך שהוא, אם יתחזק את עצמו ברצון, הינו שאפלו כשאינו זוכה להוציא מכח אל הפעל הדבר שבקדושה שחפץ לעשות או המדרגה בעבודת השם שרוצה להשיג, אוף על פי כן לבו הומה ומיחל תמיד בכל מעיו ובכל איבריו הפנימיים שלו לגמר ולעשות רצונו יתברך בבחינת: מעי מעי אוחילה, על ידי זה מרחם עליו השם יתברך ומורה לו דרך האמת לכון רצונו יתברך, עד שזוכה לחבר ספרים קדושים, לבאר דרכים ועצות איך לעשות רצונו יתברך ולבטל כל הספקות שיש לשאר בני אדם בענין עבודת השם ועשית רצונו יתברך, שזה בחינת כל ספקי דינים שיש בתורה, והעקר - לחבר ספרים קדושים, המביאים לידי מעשה ולקיום התורה. (הלכות ברכות השחר, הלכה ה' אות לז):
segments.en:
1.
In everything that passes over a person — however things may be — if he strengthens himself in will [ratzon]: that even when he does not merit to bring forth from potential to actuality the holy matter he wishes to do, or the level in the service of G-d he wishes to attain — even so, his heart yearns and hopes always in all his inward parts and all his inner limbs to complete and do His blessed will — in the aspect of: "My inward parts, my inward parts, I yearn" — through this G-d, blessed be He, has compassion upon him and shows him the path of truth to accord with His blessed will. Until he merits to compose holy books — to explain paths and counsels as to how to do His blessed will, and to nullify all the doubts that other people have in the matter of the service of G-d and the doing of His blessed will. Which is the aspect of all the doubtful laws in the Torah. And the essential [purpose] is to compose holy books that bring to action and the fulfillment of the Torah.

(Hilchos Bircas HaShachar, Halacha 5, item 37).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of the necessity of leaving the home into the outside every single time. For when one goes outside — which is the aspect of nafak — where the dominion of the outer forces resides — and when one remembers G-d even there and cleaves to Him, blessed be He — then he extracts the holiness of external places and elevates everything to holiness. And this is the aspect of: "When you sit in your home and when you walk on the way" [Deuteronomy 6:7] — the aspect of ail v'nafak.

segments.he:
ב.
בגלותנו הארך, שעובר עלינו מה שעובר בכלליות ובפרטיות צרות מצרות שונות, אשר כמעט אפס תקוה, חס ושלום על כן אין לנו עתה שום חיות, כי אם התקוה והתוחלת והרצון החזק אליו יתברך, שהוא בחינת הארת הרצון, בבחינת: מה תעירו ומה תעוררו את האהבה עד שתחפץ, כי אף על פי שנדמה כבר להסטרא אחרא שפעלה הרבה ובטלה אותנו מכמה קדושות בכלליות ובפרטיות על ידי חורבן בית המקדש ועל הגלות וכו', אוף על פי כן לא הועילה כלום, כי עדין החפץ והרצון והכסופין שלנו חזקים ותקיפים מאד אליו יתברך, ומאחר שהרצון דקדושה חזק מאד, אז בודאי לא יועילו עם כל ההסתות והפתויים והבלבולים והמניעות כי כולם יתבטלו מחמת תקף הרצון. וזה בחינת מצות חלה, שתקנו חכמינו זכרונם לברכה גם בחוץ לארץ, בכדי שלא תתבטל תורת חלה כי עקר הארת הרצון דקדושה זוכין לקבל בשעת האכילה, דעל ידי מצות חלה נתתקנת האכילה, שיזכו לקבל על ידה הארת הרצון, ועל כן נקראת חלה, מלשון תוחלת וקווי, וקווי, שהוא בחינת רצון וגעגועים, ורק זה נשאר לנו בגלותנו הארך, ועל כן חלה אין לה שעור מדאוריתא, כי הארת הרצון הוא בבחינת אין שעור, ועל כן על ידי זה דיקא יכולין להתחזק תמיד ולכבש כל המלחמות מצוה, שצריכין להלחם בזה העולם עם היצר הרע וחילותיו, והם מתגברים מאד מכל צד ורוצים להפיל את האדם גם מהרצון דקדושה, ועל כן צריכין להתחזק בזה מאד ולבלי להתיאש את עצמו בשום אפן ולהיות איש חיל להתגבר על כל פנים על כל פנים ברצונות טובים דקדושה, שעל ידי זה עקר התגברות המלחמה, כי זה נשאר קים לעולם, יהיה איך שיהיה, כי הוא דבר שאין לו שעור, וכל אחד כפי מה שהוא יוכל להתחזק בזה תמיד בכל מה שעובר עליו, כי יהיה איך שיהיה, אוף על פי כן רצונו חזק מאד אליו יתברך. (הלכות פדיון בכור, הלכה ה', אות כו', כז, ל, לב):
segments.en:
2.
In our long exile — through which what passes over us in the general and the particular passes: afflictions upon afflictions of many different kinds — so that it is almost hopeless, G-d forbid — therefore we now have no vitality whatsoever except the hope and the anticipation and the strong will toward Him, blessed be He. Which is the aspect of the illumination of will [horas haratzon]. In the aspect of: "Why do you rouse and why do you awaken the love until it pleases". For even though it already seems to the sitra achra that it has accomplished much and nullified us from many holinesses — in the general and in the particular — through the destruction of the Temple and through the exile, etc. — even so, it has accomplished nothing. For our desire and will and longing are still very strong and powerful toward Him, blessed be He. And since the holy will is very strong — then certainly all the enticements and temptations and confusions and obstacles will not avail — for they will all be nullified because of the strength of the will.

And this is the aspect of the commandment of challah — which our Sages of blessed memory ordained even in the diaspora — so that the Torah of challah should not be nullified. For the essential illumination of the holy will is received at the time of eating. For through the commandment of challah the eating is repaired — so that one merits to receive through it the illumination of will. And therefore it is called challah — from the language of anticipation [tocheiles] and hoping — and hoping — [kivui] — which is the aspect of will and longing. And only this remains for us in our long exile. And therefore challah has no Scriptural measure [ain lah shi'ur min haTorah] — for the illumination of will is in the aspect of without measure. And therefore through this specifically one can always strengthen himself and conquer all the milchemes mitzvah [obligatory battles] — that one must fight in this world with the yetzer hara and its forces. They intensify greatly from all sides and wish to cause the person to fall even from the holy will. And therefore one must strengthen himself greatly in this — and not despair of himself in any manner whatsoever. And to be a strong man — to prevail at least — at least — with holy good desires. Through which comes the essential victory of the battle. For this endures forever — however things may be. For it is a matter without measure. And each person — according to how he is — can strengthen himself in this always in whatever passes over him. For however things may be — even so, his will is very strong toward Him, blessed be He.

(Hilchos Pidyon Bechor, Halacha 5, items 26, 27, 30, 32).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of Israel walking in the desert — which is a place of outer forces, a place of serpent and fiery snake and scorpion — in order to subdue the sitra achra and to extract the holiness also from there, in the aspect of: "Fortunate is one who enters and exits." And then specifically — when they walk in the desert in outer places, which is the aspect of nafak — and when they merit to find G-d there — then specifically G-d hovers over Israel with very lofty holiness. Which is the aspect of the encompassing clouds of glory that Israel merited in the desert. Which are the aspect of sukkah — the aspect of the mother who hovers over her children [ima d'mesachcha al banin]. Which is a very lofty holiness that hovers and protects over a person specifically at the time when he is in the aspect of nafak — in order to guard him and rescue him lest he fall there, G-d — [G-d] — forbid. And helps him to subdue the sitra achra and to extract specifically from there the holiness. It is thus found that specifically through the aspect of nafak one merits a very great ascent — to the aspect of sukkah. Which is the aspect of descent being the ultimate purpose of ascent aforementioned.

segments.he:
ג.
כל המזיקי עלמא, רחמנא לצלן, עקר יניקתם מכסופין והבלים רעים, שמהם נעשין נפשות לא טובים, שהם הם המזיקין, רחמנא לצלן, כי הם מזיקין בגשמיות וברוחניות, כי הולכים ומעוררים את בני אדם לרע, חס ושלום, שמשם כל ההזקות, רחמנא לצלן ועל כן עקר הכנעתה ובטולה הוא על ידי הצדיקים והכשרים, שיש להם כסופין טובים, שהם בחינת נפשות טובים, שמעוררין העולם לטוב, שהם מכניעים ומבטלים כל המזיקי עלמא בבחינת: על שחל ופתן תדרך וכו', כי בי חשק ואפלטהו. (הלכות אמנין, הלכה ד', אות כב):
segments.en:
3.
All the damagers of the world, G-d protect us — the essential nourishment they draw from is from evil longings and breaths. From which are made evil souls — which are those very damagers, G-d protect us. For they damage physically and spiritually — for they go and arouse people toward evil, G-d forbid. From which come all the damages, G-d protect us. And therefore the essential subduing and nullification [of these damagers] is through the Tzaddikim and the upright — who have good longings, which are the aspect of good souls. Which stir the world toward good. They are the ones who subdue and nullify all the damagers of the world — in the aspect of: "You shall tread upon the lion and the serpent, etc.". "Because he cleaves to Me, I will deliver him".

(Hilchos Ominim, Halacha 4, item 22).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of the commandment of sukkah — which G-d caused us to merit at the beginning of the year, at the beginning of the teshuvah. Which must be in the aspect of ail v'nafak specifically. And the aspect of ail is fulfilled on Rosh Hashanah and the Ten Days of Repentance and Yom Kippur. And afterwards one must fulfill also the aspect of nafak — which is the aspect of the completion [tamah]: that one goes out from the home to sit in the sukkah — to show that when a person is in the aspect of nafak and seeks and — [seeks and] — searches even there to cleave to G-d — then specifically he merits very lofty holiness, the aspect of sukkah. Which is the aspect of the encompassing lights [makifim] that guard and protect the person then — when he is in the aspect of nafak.

segments.he:
ד.
צריכין לשמר עצמו מאד לבלי לדבר שום דבור רע של כסופין ורצונות רעים, חס ושלום, הבאים על לבו, רק יהפך הדבר וירגיל את עצמו לדבר בפיו תמיד כסופין טובים דקדושה, שעל ידי זה נעשין פעולות טובות בעולם, ונמשך על ידי זה כל הברכות וההשפעות, ונעשין נפשות טובים, שהולכים ומתגלגלים בעולם ומעוררים כל העולם להשם יתברך ולתורתו. (שם, אות כט):
segments.en:
4.
One must guard himself greatly — not to speak any evil word of evil longings and evil wills, G-d forbid, that come upon his heart. Rather, one should reverse the matter and train himself to speak always from his mouth good holy longings. Through which good effects are made in the world — and through this all the blessings and flows are drawn. And good souls are made — which go and circulate in the world and arouse the entire world toward G-d, blessed be He, and His Torah.

(ibid., item 29).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And through the commandment of sukkah we merit throughout the year to do — [to do] — complete teshuvah in the aspect of ail v'nafak. And at every time we are in the aspect of nafak — the sukkas shalom [shelter of peace] protects us like a mother protecting her child from falling, G-d forbid, when he walks in a dangerous place. And this is what we request specifically at night — which is the aspect of nafak, corresponding to the attribute of day — "and spread over us the shelter of Your peace." For then specifically the shelter of peace guards [us]. For the shelter of peace always guards a person at every time of danger where protection is needed — then the shelter of peace guards. And this is the aspect of: "For He will hide me in His sukkah on the day of evil" [Psalms 27:5] — specifically on the day of evil — which is the aspect of nafak — that is, at the time a person falls from his service. And when he merits to strengthen himself and not despair of himself even then — then the shelter of peace guards us as above.

segments.he: ערך שמחה
segments.en: Joy

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: All the decrees, G-d protect us, derive from sins. And the general repair [tikun hakelali] of all sins is the repair of the bris. And likewise the general repair of speech is the praise of the Tzaddikim. And the general repair of commerce is tzedakah [charity]. And this is the aspect of: "Teshuvah, prayer, and charity avert the evil of the decree" — which correspond to: fasting, voice, and money [tzom, kol, mamon]. For fasting is the aspect of the repair of the bris as above. Prayer is the aspect of the abundance of prayers and praises that one multiplies to G-d on Yom Kippur. And tzedakah is the aspect of the general repair of commerce as above.

segments.he:
א.
מי שיש לו אמונה שלמה בהשם יתברך, בודאי ראוי לשמח תמיד בהשם יתברך. וזה הדבר אי אפשר לבאר בכתב, כי הוא לכל חד כפום מה דמשער בלבה, וכן לשמח בשמחת המצוות בחינת: פקודי השם ישרים משמחי לב, כי בודאי אין שמחה בעולם כשמחה זו, כי זה כל אדם יכול להבין, שבעולם הזה אין שום שמחה בעולם, כי מה יתרון לו לאדם וכו', וימינו כצל עובר, ואחרית שמחה - תוגה, ועל כן באמת המחקרים והכופרים, רחמנא לצלן, אין להם שום שמחה אמתית כלל, וכל ימיהם הם מלאים עצבות ויגון ואנחה, כי מאחר שכופרים בתורתו הקדושה ובעשית מצוותיו יתברך ובודים מלבם טעמים של הבל ושטות על עשית המצוות כאלו הם נימוסיות, חס ושלום, אם כן מהיכן יקבלו חיות ושמחה, ועל כן עקר הקטרוג וההתגרות של הסטרא אחרא שמתגרין בישראל, העקר הוא בשמחה של המצוות, כי על גוף המצוה הם יכולין לומר שהיא נימוסיות, חס ושלום, כשאר נימוסי נימוסי העמים, חס ושלום, אך כשרואים שישראל שמחים כל כך בעשית המצוות ומוסרין נפשם עליהם, על זה הם מתקנאים ומתגרים בנו מאד, ועל כן עקר הכנעת הסטרא אחרא היא דיקא על ידי עשית המצוה בשמחה. (הלכות נפילת אפים, הלכה ד', אות ד):
segments.en:
1.
One who has complete faith in G-d, blessed be He — certainly he is fitting to always rejoice in G-d, blessed be He. And this matter is impossible to explain in writing — for it is for each person according to what he measures in his own heart. And likewise to rejoice in the joy of the commandments — in the aspect of: "The precepts of G-d are upright, gladdening the heart". For certainly there is no joy in the world like this joy. For this every person can understand: that in this world there is no joy whatsoever. For "what advantage has a person, etc.?" — "and our days are like a passing shadow" — and "in the end of joy is sorrow".

And therefore in truth the philosophers and the heretics, G-d protect us, have no true joy whatsoever — and all their days are full of sadness and sorrow and sighing. For since they deny His holy Torah and the doing of His blessed commandments — and fabricate from their hearts reasons of vanity and foolishness about the doing of the commandments, as if they are merely conventional [nimmusiyos], G-d forbid — if so, from where will they receive vitality and joy? And therefore the essential accusation and provocation of the sitra achra that provokes against Israel — the essential [one] is in the joy of the commandments. For regarding the body of the commandment — they can say that it is conventional, G-d forbid, like the conventions of — [the conventions of] — the nations, G-d forbid. But when they see that Israel rejoices so greatly in the doing of the commandments and gives their lives for them — for this they are very envious and provoke us greatly. And therefore the essential subduing of the sitra achra is specifically through the doing of the commandment with joy.

(Hilchos Nefilas Apayim, Halacha 4, item 4).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: A person must know and believe that G-d makes new things at every time — and no day is like another, how much more so that no year is like another. And in every day — and especially in every single year — everything is renewed entirely. And certainly G-d and the Tzaddikim will complete what they have begun. And if in the meanwhile what passes over us in the general and the particular passes over us — and the sitra achra and the baal davar spreads lengthwise and widthwise every single time — even so G-d helps us every day. And especially each year — when we receive the holiness of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur until Simchas Torah. And then the Torah is completed and we begin it again. And in each year new repairs are completed for each person — in a manner that every person can always be renewed for the good. As long as he believes in the truth: that G-d in His goodness each day always renews the act of creation. Especially each and every year. Until in the end the repair will be completed in perfection through our righteous Mashiach — may he come speedily in our days.

segments.he:
ב.
העולם הזה הוא מלא כעס ומכאובות ויגון ואנחה, וכל חיותנו וקיומנו הוא רק על ידי בחינת שבת, שהוא עלמא דאתי, כי רק זה כל תכליתנו, כי בודאי לא ברא השם יתברך את האדם בחכמה נפלאה ונוראה כזאת בשביל שיסבל עמל וכעס כזה בזה העולם, כי כונת השם יתברך בודאי רק לטובה, וכל הבריאה היתה בשביל לגלות רחמנותו וטובו, אך עקר בריאת האדם הוא רק בשביל התכלית, שהוא בחינת שבת, וזה כל הנחמה על כל הצרות והיגונות שסובל האדם בזה העולם, ועל כן צריכין להתגבר מאד בכל עת להמשיך שמחה על עצמו, והעקר - על ידי שיסתכל על הסוף, שהוא תכלית עולם הבא, שאז יתהפך הכל לטובה, כי אפלו הפחות שבישראל והגרוע שבגרועים - אין שעור לכל נעימות הטוב הנפלא שיזכה שיזכה אז, ועל ידי זה יוכל לשמח את עצמו גם עתה בכל מה שעובר עליו, עד שיזכה על ידי זה ליצא מן גלותו מהיכלי התמורותויזכה לכל טוב. (הלכות ברכות הודאה, הלכה ו', אות ט י):
segments.en:
2.
This world is full of anger and pain and sorrow and sighing. And all our vitality and our endurance is only through the aspect of Shabbos — which is the World to Come. For this is our entire purpose. For certainly G-d, blessed be He, did not create man with such wondrous and awesome wisdom for the purpose of enduring such toil and anger in this world. For the intention of G-d, blessed be He, is certainly only for the good — and all of the creation was for the purpose of revealing His compassion and His goodness. But the essential creation of man is only for the sake of the purpose [tachlis] — which is the aspect of Shabbos. And this is all the consolation for all the afflictions and sorrows a person endures in this world. And therefore one must strengthen oneself greatly at all times to draw joy upon oneself. And the essential [way] is: through gazing at the end — which is the purpose of the World to Come. For then everything will be transformed for good. For even the least of Israel and the worst of the worst — beyond measure is all the pleasantness of the wondrous good that he will merit — [that he will merit] — then. And through this one can also gladden himself now through whatever passes over him — until he merits through this to emerge from his exile from the palaces of substitution — and to merit all good.

(Hilchos Bircas HaHodaah, Halacha 6, items 9–10).

history.en: At the resting place of the Tzaddikim in their holy graves — there the holiness of the Throne of Glory [kise hakavod] is drawn — which is their inheritance. As it is written: "And a glorious throne shall He cause them to inherit" [I Samuel 2:8]. And therefore there are included all the places of every single person — and every single person can find his place there, until he merits through this to return to G-d. Because there shines the holiness of the aspect of mekomo shel olam [the place of the world] — which is the root of all places. And there every person can find the beginning and the starting point from which he must begin to return to G-d. And for this reason people travel to the graves of the Tzaddikim on the eve of Rosh Hashanah.

segments.he:
ג.
מי שלבו שלם עם השם ואמונתו חזקה ומאמין שהכל ברצונו יתברך, אזי הוא בשמחה תמיד ואין לו שום דאגה ופחד כלל משום דבר שבעולם בבחינת: אל תירא מפחד פתאם וכו', כי מאחר שהכל רק ברצונו יתברך, אם כן אין לו להתירא משום דבר, כי מי יוכל לעשות לו דבר גדול או דבר קטן בלי רצונו יתברך, כמו שכתוב: השם לי לא אירא וכו', ועל כן הוא שמח תמיד, ואפלו אם לפעמים באין עליו איזה יסורים, חס ושלום, אוף על פי כן מאחר שיודע שהכל ברצונו יתברך לבד, הוא יכול לשמח את עצמו תמיד, כי כונת השם יתברך, שמביא עליו היסורין, הוא בודאי רק לטובה: אם להזכירו שישוב בתשובה, בתשובה, אם למרק עוונותיו, ואם כן כל היסורים, חס ושלום, הם טובות גדולות, ועל כן הוא יכול לשמח את עצמו תמיד, כי יודע שהשם יתברך מלא רחמים, וכונתו יתברך בודאי לטובה, ולא לעולם יריב וכו', ובודאי ישוב השם וירחמהו וייטיב אחריתו, והיסורים יתהפכו לו לטובה גדולה לעולמי עד ולנצח נצחים, ועל כן הוא בשמחה תמיד אבל מי שנוטה, חס ושלום מאמונה וטועה, חס ושלום, בכפירות של חכמי הטבע וסובר שיש טבע, חס ושלום - אזי אין לו שום חיים כלל, כי כל ימיו כעס ומכאובות, וכל ימי רשע הוא מתחולל וכו' בשלום שודד יבואנו, כי מתירא פן יבוא עליו שבר פתאם, וכשבא עליו איזה צרה ויסורין, אין לו למי לפנות להושע, ועל כן הוא מלא צער ויסורין ופחדים ועצבות תמיד, ואין לו שום חיים כלל, וכמבאר במקום אחר אבל מי שיש לו אמונה שלמה ברצון, שיודע שהכל רק ברצונו יתברך, אזי זוכה לשמחה גדולה, וכל היראות והופחדים שיש לו מאיזה דבר שבעולם, כולם נתהפכין לשמחה גדולה, כי על ידי זה הוא חוזר להשם יתברך ויודע שהכל לטובה כנ"ל. (הלכות כלי היין, הלכה א', אות א):
segments.en:
3.
One whose heart is whole with G-d — and whose faith is strong — and who believes that everything is through His blessed will — he is in joy always. And has no worry or fear at all from any matter in the world. In the aspect of: "Do not fear a sudden terror, etc.". For since everything is only through His blessed will — he has nothing to fear from any matter. For who can do to him anything great or anything small without His blessed will? As it is written: "G-d is for me, I will not fear, etc.". And therefore he is always in joy. And even if sometimes some sufferings come upon him, G-d forbid — even so, since he knows that everything is through His blessed will alone — he can always gladden himself. For the intention of G-d, blessed be He, in bringing upon him the sufferings is certainly only for the good: whether to remind him to return in teshuvah — [in teshuvah] — or to scour his sins. And if so — all the sufferings, G-d forbid, are great goodnesses. And therefore he can always gladden himself — for he knows that G-d, blessed be He, is full of compassion, and His blessed intention is certainly for the good. And "He will not contend forever, etc.". And certainly G-d will return and have compassion upon him and improve his end — and the sufferings will be transformed for him into very great goodness for all eternity and for everlasting ever. And therefore he is always in joy.

But one who deviates, G-d forbid, from faith — and errs, G-d forbid, in the heresies of the naturalistic philosophers — and believes there is nature, G-d forbid — then he has no life at all. For all his days [are] anger and pain — and "all the days of the wicked he writhes, etc.". "In peace — ruin will come upon him". For he fears lest sudden destruction come upon him. And when some affliction and suffering comes upon him — he has no one to turn to for salvation. And therefore he is full of sorrow and suffering and fears and sadness always — and has no life at all. And as is explained elsewhere. But one who has complete faith in the will — who knows that everything is only through His blessed will — he merits great joy. And all the fears and dreads he has from any matter in the world — they are all transformed into great joy. For through this he returns to G-d, blessed be He, and knows that everything is for the good as above.

(Hilchos K'lai HaYayin, Halacha 1, item 1).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: On Rosh Hashanah G-d has compassion upon us and judges us to the scale of merit — each person according to his place. And through this we truly enter into the scale of merit — until through this we merit to cry out to G-d from the depths of the heart and to return in teshuvah before Him, blessed be He. And afterwards — on Hoshana Rabbah, at the end of Sukkos — through meriting to sit in the sukkah, which is the aspect of the Throne of Glory, mekomo shel olam — through this all of Israel merits to receive illumination from there. Until we all merit this aspect: to fulfill: "Do not judge your fellow until you have reached his place" [Avos 2:5]. And to know to judge everyone to the scale of merit — even the sinners of Israel — until we merit to bring them all into the scale of merit and to shine upon them the illumination of Rosh Hashanah. That is, that all of them will always find a door and a path of teshuvah in every place they are, at every time.

segments.he: ערך תלמוד תורה
segments.en: Torah Study

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And the essential door and path is to always cry out to G-d from the depths of the heart — however things may be — and to never despair of the cry. Which is the aspect of the abundance of cries that one multiplies on Hoshana Rabbah — crying out many, many times: Hoshana! And one stays awake the entire night and completes the book of Psalms — which is full of cries and wails and pleas, etc., to G-d. Until there is no person in the world who cannot find himself in the book of Psalms — which encompasses all who come into the world in all generations and at all levels in the world down to the very lowest possible level — and stirs them all to return to G-d. For Psalms is a segula for teshuvah.

segments.he:
א.
למוד התורה שלומדין בלילה הוא קרוב יותר לעלות אל השכינה, הן מצד האדם, הן מצד השכינה, כביכול, כי האדם יכול לבטל את עצמו ולדבק את עצמו בו יתברך בלילה יותר מביום, מחמת שאז העולם ניח קצת מרדיפת העולם הזה, וגם השכינה היא סמוכה להאדם הלומד בלילה ומקשבת לקולו, כמו שכתוב: קומי רני בלילה וכו' נכח פני השם - נכח פני השם דיקא, כי השכינה קרובה אליו, והוא נכח פני השם ממש, כי בלילה השכינה היא בעולמות התחתונים, ואז עקר מנוחתה אצל האדם הלומד אז. (הלכות תפלה, הלכה א'):
segments.en:
1.
The study of Torah that one studies at night is closer to ascending toward the Shechinah — both from the person's side and from the Shechinah's side, as it were. For a person can nullify himself and cleave to Him, blessed be He, at night more than by day — because then the world rests somewhat from the pursuit of this world. And the Shechinah too is close to the person who studies at night and attends to his voice. As it is written: "Rise, cry out in the night, etc. — directly before the face of G-d" — specifically directly before the face of G-d. For the Shechinah is close to him — and he is directly before the face of G-d literally. For at night the Shechinah is in the lower worlds — and then the essential resting of the Shechinah is with the person who studies then.

(Hilchos Tefilah, Halacha 1).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And on Hoshana Rabbah we draw this wondrous path — that every person of Israel should merit through the holiness of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur and Sukkos — to judge everything to the scale of merit, and to bring the paths of teshuvah into every single person of Israel: that is, to say Psalms and to cry out to G-d always, however things may be. And likewise one must judge even himself to the scale of merit and fulfill in himself: "Do not judge, etc., until you have reached his place." For certainly even his own place — he does not know from where it is drawn. And whatever passed over him in all his gilgulim [reincarnations], and from where his evil desires and evil thoughts derive, etc. Therefore it is forever forbidden to despair of oneself. For one must fulfill in oneself as well: "Do not be contemptuous of any person" — which is the aspect of the prohibition of bloodshed [shfichus damim], as explained in the inner teachings. For a person is warned against the prohibition of bloodshed also regarding his own soul. As it is written: "But your blood of your own lives, etc." [Genesis 9:5] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "This refers to one who spills his own blood." For even to hold oneself in too much contempt — to the point that he could fall even more through this, G-d forbid — this is certainly a severe prohibition. For one must judge even oneself to the scale of merit — for who knows his own place?

segments.he:
ב.
עקר הטהרה מהבגדים הצואים הנאחזים בכל אחד, שמהם כל המניעות והעכובים מעבודת השם, עקר הטהרה מהם היא על ידי התורה הקדושה, שנקראת באר מים חיים ונהר שאינו פוסק ומעין המתגבר, כי אלו הבגדים הצואים, שיש לכל אדם כל זמן שלא תקן חטאיו, ובפרט מי שנתלכלך כמו שנתלכלך, רחמנא לצלן, שעל ידי זה מתעוררין ומתגברין עליו המניעות והמסכים בכל פעם ומשתטחים לפניו ומפסיקים מאד מאד בינו לבין הקדושה כמו נהר המפסיק ממש, ואלו הבגדים הצואים הם בחינת יון מצולה, בחינת טיט היון, שמתדבק מאד בכל פעם, ומשם באים כל הנפילות וההתרחקות של הרבה בני אדם מהשם יתברך, כי אפלו אם מתעורר לפעמים לשוב להשם יתברך - תכף משתטחים כנגדו ואינם מניחים אותו להתקרב, וכן בכל פעם ועל ועל זה צעק דוד המלך, עליו השלום, בשביל כלל ישראל: טבעתי ביון מצולה ואין מעמד וכו', הצילני מטיט ואל אטבעה וכו'. ועקר התקון לזה היא התורה הקדושה, כי התורה היא מקור מים חיים, שמטהרת מכל הגלולים והטנופים בחינת: וזרקתי עליכם מים טהורים וכו'. וזה צריך כל אדם לידע, שאפלו אם הוא כמו שהוא, אם יברח בכל פעם אל התורה, הן הרבה או מעט על כל פנים, אם אי אפשר לו מחמת פרנסה או שאר מניעות, על כל פנים כשיקבוע עצמו על התורה ללמד בכל יום איך שיהיה ויעבר עליו מה, אזי בודאי סוף כל סוף יהיה נטהר מכל הבגדים הצואים ויתקרב להשם יתברך באמת, כי אף על פי שהם נסבבים מאד בהאדם, ובכל פעם שמתעורר האדם להשם יתברך הם מתגברים ביותר, וכמובא בכתבי האר"י זכרונו לברכה, שיש שהמצולות ים, שהם ההרהורים רעים ומגונים, מתגברים עליהם ביותר, בפרט בעת עסקם בתורה ותפלה, אבל אוף על פי כן אם לא יניח את מקומו ויכריח מחשבתו להמשיכה לתוך תורה ותפלה בכל פעם, יהיה איך שיהיה, בודאי סוף כל סוף התורה תטהר אותו מכל הנ"ל, כי התורה היא בחינת נהר שאינו פוסק וכו', שאין שום טומאה ולכלוך יכול להתקים כנגדה, כי כל הטומאות והגלולים היא שוטפת אותם ומבטלת אותם ברגע קלה רק שהעקר - שיהיה חזק בזה, כי אחר כך הם חוזרים ומתגברים ביותר, וצריך לחזר ולברח אל התורה, וכן בכל פעם. וזה בחינת קבעת עתים לתורה, קבעת דיקא, שיהיה עסק התורה אצלו בקביעות גדול, אפלו מי שאינו עוסק בתורה כל היום כי אם איזה עתים ושעות, על כל פנים צריך לזהר שיהיה אלו העתים והשעות בקביעות גדול בכל יום, חק ולא יעבר! כדי שיברח בכל פעם למקור מים החיים, המטהרים מכל הטומאות והבגדים הצואים כנ"ל. (הלכות בציעת הפת, הלכה ה', אות ג):
segments.en:
2.
The essential purification from the soiled garments [begodim tzo'im] that cling to every person — from which come all the obstacles and hindrances from the service of G-d — the essential purification from them is through the holy Torah. Which is called a well of living waters, and a never-ceasing river, and a strengthening fountain. For these soiled garments — which every person has for as long as he has not repaired his sins, and especially one who has become soiled as he has become soiled, G-d protect us — through this the obstacles and screens are aroused and intensified over him every single time and spread before him. And interrupt very — [very] — greatly between him and holiness — like a river that literally cuts off. And these soiled garments are the aspect of the sinking mire — the aspect of tit hayaven [deep mire] — that clings greatly every single time. And from there come all the falls and the distancing of many people from G-d, blessed be He. For even if he is sometimes awakened to return to G-d, blessed be He — immediately they spread against him and do not allow him to draw close. And so every single time. And for — [for] — this King David, peace be upon him, cried out on behalf of all of Israel: "I have sunk in deep mire and there is no foothold, etc. — rescue me from the mire, and let me not sink, etc.".

And the essential repair for this is the holy Torah. For the Torah is a source of living water — that purifies from all pollutions and filths — in the aspect of: "And I will sprinkle upon you pure water, etc.". And this every person must know: that even if he is as he is — if he flees every single time to the Torah — whether much or little at least — even if it is impossible for him because of livelihood or other obstacles — at the very least when he establishes himself upon Torah — to study each and every day however things may be and whatever may pass over him — then certainly in the end he will be purified from all the soiled garments and will draw close to G-d, blessed be He, in truth. For even though they encircle the person greatly — and every single time a person is awakened toward G-d, blessed be He, they intensify even more — as is brought in the writings of the Arizal, of blessed memory: that there are those over whom the depths of the sea [metzulos yam] — which are the evil and shameful thoughts — intensify even more, especially at the time of their engaging in Torah and prayer. But even so — if he does not abandon his place and forces his thought to draw it into Torah and prayer every single time — however things may be — certainly in the end the Torah will purify him from all the aforementioned. For the Torah is the aspect of a never-ceasing river, etc. — that no impurity or filth can endure against it. For all the impurities and pollutions it sweeps away and nullifies them in an instant. Only the essential thing is that he be strong in this — for afterwards they return and intensify even more. And he must return and flee to the Torah. And so every single time. And this is the aspect of: kova'as itim l'Torah — kava'as specifically — that his engagement in Torah be with great regularity, even for one who engages in Torah only some times and hours and not all day. At the very least he must be careful that these times and hours be with great regularity each and every day — a statute not to be crossed! In order to flee every single time to the source of living water that purifies from all the impurities and soiled garments as above.

(Hilchos Betziyas HaPas, Halacha 5, item 3).

history.en: And the essential thing: do not despair yourself of the cry — ever. And cry out and implore before G-d always from the depths of the heart — in the aspect of: "Pour out your heart like water before the face of G-d" [Lamentations 2:19]. Through which we will all merit to return to Him, blessed be He. And all of this we engage in drawing [l'hamshich] on Hoshana Rabbah. And therefore we engage then with the willow branches [aravei nachal] — which allude to the sinners of Israel — to fulfill in them also: "Do not be contemptuous of any person" — and to judge them to the scale of merit. And this is the aspect of what is said on Hoshana Rabbah — Mishneh Torah — which revolves and orbits entirely around this very axis: to warn Israel that in all that passes over them, etc. — even so, they should never despair of themselves from the cry. For G-d will not abandon His people — and His compassion never ends. And after all the sins and provocations with which they provoke before Him, blessed be He, in every generation — even so, the right hand of G-d is exalted. And therefore one can always draw close and return to Him, blessed be He, from whatever place one is.

segments.he:
ג.
יש חמשים שערי קדושה וארבעים ותשעה שערים יכולין להשיג, והשער החמשים נאמר עליו: ותחסרהו מעט מאלקים, כי הוא בחינת במופלא ממנו, ואי אפשר להשיגו. וכן להפך, יש חמשים שערי טומאה, וכשלב האדם בוער אפלו אל הקדושה חוץ מהמדה, שזה בחינת שרוצה לכנס במדרגה שהיא בחינת במופלא ממנו, ואז הוא בבחינת שרוצה להשיג מה שהיא בחינת שער החמשים כפי מדרגתו, ואז רבוי האור גורם שבירת כלים, חס ושלום, שמשם עקר יניקת הטומאה, ועל ידי זה יוכל לפל לגמרי לההפך ממש, לבחינת החמימות דסטרא אחרא, שהוא בחינת תבערת הלב ביותר לכל התאוות רעות שהם מבחינת החמשים שערי טומאה, רחמנא לצלן וזה בחינת: יעלו שמים ירדו תהומות, שמחמת שהעליה הוא שלא כסדר, על כן גם הירידה עד התהום, חס ושלום וזה בחינת: פן יהרסו לעלות אל השם ונפל וכו', וזה בחינת: אל תצדק הרבה ואל תרשע הרבה ועל ידי התורה, שנתנה ביום החמשים, על ידי זה יוצאין מחמשים שערי טומאה לחמשים שערי קדושה, כי על ידי התורה מקררין שני מיני חמימות הנ"ל, כי על ידי התורה מצמצמין האור של שער החמשים וממשיכין ממנו הארה גדולה לארבעים ותשעה שערי קדושה, שזה בחינת: מזוקק שבעתים, הנאמר בתורה, וכן על ידי התורה משברין ומבטלין השער החמשים של הטומאה, ואזי ממילא בטלין כל הארבעים ותשעה שערי טומאה שיניקתם משער החמשים שלהם, ואז נתבררין כל ניצוצות הקדושה מהחמשים שערי טומאה ונכללין בחמשים שערי קדושה, כי עוונות נתהפכין לזכויות, ואז נעשה מהם בחינת מאה שערים, בחינת מאה ברכות, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות תרומות ומעשרות, הלכה ג', אות ד, ז ח):
segments.en:
3.
There are fifty gates of holiness and forty-nine gates that can be attained. And the fiftieth gate — concerning it it is said: "and You have made him slightly less than G-d" — for it is the aspect of "in what is too wondrous for him" — and it is impossible to attain. And likewise the reverse — there are fifty gates of impurity. And when a person's heart blazes even toward holiness beyond the measure — which is the aspect of wishing to enter a level that is the aspect of "in what is too wondrous for him" for his own level — and then he is in the aspect of wishing to attain what is the aspect of the fiftieth gate according to his level — then the abundance of light causes the shattering of the vessels [sheviras hakelim], G-d forbid. From which comes the essential nourishment of impurity. And through this he can fall entirely into the reverse — into the aspect of the blazing of the heart of the sitra achra — which is the aspect of the heart burning excessively toward all evil desires. Which are the aspect of the fifty gates of impurity, G-d protect us.

And this is the aspect of: "They ascend to the heavens and descend to the depths" — since the ascent is not in the proper order — therefore also the descent is to the depths, G-d forbid. And this is the aspect of: "Lest they breach [their boundary] to ascend to G-d and fall, etc.". And this is the aspect of: "Do not be overly righteous, and do not be overly wicked".

And through the Torah — which was given on the fiftieth day — through this one exits from the fifty gates of impurity to the fifty gates of holiness. For through the Torah one cools both types of blazing aforementioned. For through the Torah one compresses the light of the fiftieth gate and draws from it a great illumination to the forty-nine gates of holiness — which is the aspect of: "refined sevenfold" — said of the Torah. And likewise through the Torah one shatters and nullifies the fiftieth gate of impurity. And then automatically all the forty-nine gates of impurity are nullified — whose nourishment derives from their fiftieth gate. And then all the holy sparks are extracted from the fifty gates of impurity and encompassed within the fifty gates of holiness. For "sins are transformed into merits." And then from them is made the aspect of one hundred gates — the aspect of one hundred blessings — as explained within [the cited work].

(Hilchos Terumos U'Ma'asros, Halacha 3, items 4, 7–8).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The essential joining of two things that are very far from one another — which are like two opposites — the essential joining of them is through melody [nigun] — as explained in the inner teachings. And therefore the essential attachment [devekus] to G-d from this very low and physical and lowly world is through melody and song. As one can see plainly: that even a person who is very far from G-d and is on the very lowest rung — even so, most of the time through melody he is awakened toward G-d and reminds himself where he stands in the world. Only one must be careful not to hear melody from wicked and frivolous musicians — who are very commonly found now. For this can harm him, G-d forbid, very greatly. But through melody from people who are truly upright — who direct their hearts in truth toward G-d — or when one plays some melody oneself and his intention is for the sake of Heaven — one can be awakened through this very greatly toward G-d.

segments.he:
ד.
עקר הפגם של עץ הדעת טוב ורע היה, שלא כללו בחינת למדן וצדיק, יחד, שזהו בחינת הפגם של הלומדים החולקים על הצדיקים, שאומרים, שעקר הוא רק הלמוד בעצמו, ואין צריכים להתקרב להצדיקים ולתקן מעשיהם כלל, ולבסוף זה וזה לא עלתה בידם, כי אחר כך משליכין גם למוד התורה אחרי גום, כמצוי, בעוונותינו הרבים, בכמה אנשים, שבימי נעוריהם עסקו בתורה קצת ואחר כך פרקו על תורה לגמרי וגם קלקלו מעשיהם יותר מעמי הארץ, וכל זה - מחמת שלא השגיחו על תקון מעשיהם כלל ולא השתדלו להתקרב לצדיקי אמת ואמרו שעקר הוא הלמוד, ולבסוף זה וזה לא נתקימו בידם, כי באמת עקר תקון למוד התורה הוא על ידי בחינת צדיק, ומי שמפריד בחינת למדן מבחינת צדיק הוא בחינת אחר, שקצץ בנטיעות, כי תכלית תורה - תשובה ומעשים טובים, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, וכשהלמדן כפוף להצדיק, אזי זוכה לציר אותיות התורה לטוב על ידי כח הצדיק, שהוא הרב האמת, כמבאר בפנים, אבל כשאינו כפוף תחתיו, ומכל שכן כשחולק עליו, חס ושלום, אזי: לא זכה - נעשית לו סם מות, כי מציר אותיות התורה להפך, להפך, חס ושלום, על ידי שמפריד בין בחינת למדן לבחינת צדיק, כי עקר ציור אותיות התורה לטוב, שיהיו בבחינת סם חיים, הוא רק על ידי הצדיק האמת, שזכה לשמירת הברית בתכלית השלמות ואפלו מי שאינו זוכה לזה שיהיה הוא בעצמו בבחינת צדיק בשלמות, אוף על פי כן אם הוא מכניע את עצמו על כל פנים תחת הצדיק כעבד תחת אדוניו, אזי כל תורתו ולמודו וכל מעשיו מקבלים תקון על ידי הצדיק האמת, שמציר הכל לטוב, ואזי נאמר עליו גם כן: זכה - נעשית לו סם חיים, על ידי כח הצדיק. (הלכות אמנין, הלכה ד', אות כג):
segments.en:
4.
The essential blemish of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil was — that the aspects of lamdan [scholar] and Tzadik were not united together. Which is the aspect of the blemish of those scholars who dispute the Tzaddikim — who say that the essential thing is only the study itself, and that there is no need to draw close to the Tzaddikim and to repair one's deeds at all. And in the end — both this and that eluded them. For afterwards they also threw off Torah study entirely — as is found, in our many sins, in many people who in their youth engaged in Torah somewhat, and afterwards removed the yoke of Torah entirely and also corrupted their deeds more than those unlearned in Torah. And all of this — because they paid no attention at all to the repair of their deeds and did not strive to draw close to the truly righteous Tzaddikim. And said that the essential thing is the study. And in the end — both this and that were not sustained in their hands.

For in truth the essential repair of Torah study is through the aspect of Tzadik. And one who separates the aspect of lamdan from the aspect of Tzadik — he is the aspect of Acher [the one who went astray] — who cut down the shoots [katzatz b'neti'os]. For the purpose of Torah is repentance and good deeds — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And when the scholar bows himself before the Tzadik — then he merits to form the letters of the Torah for good through the power of the Tzadik who is the true master — as explained in the inner teachings. But when he is not subject to him — and certainly when he disputes him, G-d forbid — then: "if he has not merited — it becomes for him a deadly poison." For he forms the letters of the Torah in the reverse — [the reverse] — G-d forbid. Through separating between the aspect of lamdan and the aspect of Tzadik. For the essential forming of the letters of the Torah for good — that they be in the aspect of a life-giving remedy [sam chayyim] — is only through the true Tzadik who has merited the guarding of the bris to the ultimate perfection. And even one who does not merit that he himself should be in the aspect of Tzadik in perfection — even so, if he humbles himself at least before the Tzadik — like a servant before his master — then all his Torah and study and all his deeds receive repair through the true Tzadik, who forms everything for good. And then it is said of him also: "If he has merited — it becomes for him a life-giving remedy" — through the power of the Tzadik.

(Hilchos Ominim, Halacha 4, item 23).

history.en: For the essential joining and attachment from this world — the physical world — to G-d — who is immeasurably exalted and elevated — especially for one who has sinned and been greatly distanced from his Father in Heaven — is through melody and song. Which is the aspect of all the songs and praises spoken to G-d. And for this reason King David, peace be upon him, composed the entire book of Psalms — which encompasses all ten types of melody. For he is the aspect of Mashiach — who engages in repairing the blemish of the broken Tablets. Through which all the destructions came. And David — who is Mashiach — who engages in repairing this, which is the repair of all the worlds — therefore composed the book of Psalms encompassing all ten types of melody. For through the ten types of melody the broken Tablets are repaired. For through melody for the sake of Heaven — one attaches and joins the heart to G-d from wherever one is. Until one can receive the light of the letters of the Torah — in the aspect of: "write them upon the tablet of your heart" [Proverbs 3:3]. And likewise — commensurate with how much the heart is drawn after G-d — so too there is the power for the Tablets to bear the light of the letters of the Torah. Which is the aspect of the repair of the broken Tablets — which came about through the aspect of the letters flying off, as our Sages of blessed memory said.

segments.he: ערך תפלה
segments.en: Prayer

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the aspect of: "Bind them upon your throat" [Proverbs 3:3] — specifically [davka] — the aspect of the throat and larynx from which the voice emerges. There should be bound in it the words of Torah. That is, his melody should be for the sake of Heaven. And through this: "write them upon the tablet of your heart" — as above. And through this one merits to be saved from the forgetting of Torah — and merits to see the light of Torah in perfection in the aspect of a life-giving remedy [sam chayyim].

segments.he:
א.
קימת חצות או על כל פנים קדם אור היום לעסק בתורה, על ידי זה זוכין לידע בידיעה שלמה שמלא כל הארץ כבודו, ועל ידי זה זוכין להתפלל בכונה גדולה, כי כשיודע שהשם יתברך עומד עליו ושומע ומאזין ומקשיב כל דבור ודבור שיוצא מפיו, בודאי יתלהב לבו מאד בתפלתו וידקדק מאד לכון דבריו ולידיעה זו זוכין על ידי קימת חצות, כנזכר לעיל. (הלכות השכמת הבקר, הלכה ג', אות ד):
segments.en:
1.
Rising at midnight [chatzos] — or at the very least before dawn — to engage in Torah: through this one merits to know with complete knowledge that "the whole earth is full of His glory". And through this one merits to pray with great intention. For when one knows that G-d, blessed be He, stands over him and hears and listens and attends to every single word that comes out of his mouth — certainly his heart will be greatly inflamed in his prayer, and he will take great care to direct his words. And one merits this knowledge through rising at midnight, as mentioned above.

(Hilchos Hashkomas HaBoker, Halacha 3, item 4).
