requiredNotes.text: The source reads על יד על ידי, an interrupted and replayed phrase. The English “on account of — [on account of]” preserves that repetition rather than editing the Hebrew.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The essential [work of the] yetzer hara — which intensifies in every generation — is to hide and conceal the true Tzadik of this very generation. As is plainly visible: the essential controversy is against the Tzadik of that very generation. And afterwards — in the days that come — the world acknowledges also this Tzadik and says that he was certainly a Tzadik. Only they dispute the Tzadik of this very generation. As we saw regarding the controversy that existed against the Arizal, of blessed memory, in his own days — and afterwards all acknowledged the holiness of the Arizal and disputed the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory — and so in every generation. And all of this — because the essential clarification [birur] of the imagination — through which one merits complete faith — is specifically through this very true Tzadik of this very generation.

segments.he: ערך תשובה
segments.en: Repentance

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore the baal davar allows itself to spread lengthwise and widthwise to hide and conceal this specific Tzadik. And therefore every person must strive and draw close to the true Tzadik of this very generation — specifically. In order to merit through him specifically the perfection of the clarification of faith — as is needed for this very generation and time and moment — specifically now.

segments.he:
א.
מי שהוא במדרגה תחתונה, צריך דיקא למצא זכות בעצמו, כדי שלא יפל לגמרי, חס ושלום, ועקר טהרתו ותשובתו על ידי זה דיקא, וזה בחינת טהרת הפרה אדומה. (הלכות השכמת הבקר, הלכה א', אות יב):
segments.en:
1.
One who is on a low level — he must specifically find merit in himself — so as not to fall entirely, G-d forbid. And the essential purification and repentance of such a person is specifically through this. And this is the aspect of the purification of the parah adumah [the red heifer].

(Hilchos Hashkomas HaBoker, Halacha 1, item 12).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One who separates himself from the Tzadik — he is the aspect of a dry tree [etz yaveish]. For even if he innovates some innovation in Torah — it is not considered the making of fruit at all. For it is impossible to succeed in Torah and to make true fruit — except when one binds oneself to the true Tzadik. Through which one merits good longings, and good deeds, and true Torah innovations.

segments.he:
ב.
עקר התשובה הוא לשוב מגדלות, שמזה באים כל החטאים, חס ושלום, ולהשפיל עצמו ולהרגיש שפלותו ופחיתותו באמת, כי עקר התשובה היא ההכנעה והשפלות ולב נשבר לפני השם יתברך, על ידי זה מוחל לו על כל החטאים ונתבטלים ממנו כל הדינים. (הלכות נטילת ידים שחרית, הלכה ג', אות ה):
segments.en:
2.
The essential teshuvah is to return from pride — from which come all the sins, G-d forbid. And to humble oneself and feel one's lowliness and insignificance in truth. For the essential teshuvah is the submission and the lowliness and a broken heart before G-d (blessed be He). Through this He forgives him for all the sins — and all the judgments are nullified from him.

(Hilchos Netilas Yodayim Shacharis, Halacha 3, item 5).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One who wishes to have consideration for his life — to rescue his soul from eternal death — and to be saved from the aspect of death [sitra d'musa], which is the aspect of heresies [kefirot] — and to merit complete faith, which is the very essence of life — must journey and come to the Tzaddikim and those attached to them. Which is the secret of the forty-eight cities of refuge [arei miklat] — in which the priests and the Levites dwelt. And where the killer was required to flee and escape. And these forty-eight cities correspond to the forty-eight words of the verse of Shma Yisroel — which is the foundation of the holy faith.

segments.he:
ג.
אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, שעל עוון החמור הוצאת זרע לבטלה, רחמנא לצלן, אין מועיל לו תשובה, ובאמת כך ראוי לו, כמבאר בפנים, אבל באמת אוף על פי כן אין לך דבר שעומד בפני התשובה, אך עקר תשובתו הוא על ידי הצדיק הדור, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות תפלין, הלכה ב', אות יא):
segments.en:
3.
Our Sages of blessed memory said that for the severe sin of wasting seed, G-d protect us — teshuvah is not effective for it. And in truth this is fitting for it — as explained in the inner teachings. But in truth even so — there is nothing that stands before teshuvah. Only his essential repentance is through the Tzadik of the generation — as is explained in the inner teachings.

(Hilchos Tefillin, Halacha 2, item 11).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend." And it is brought in the sacred books that this alludes to the reed [kaneh] and the quill [kulmus] with which the holy books are written. And this: "Make for yourself a teacher" — and if you cannot find him, then the remedy is through: "and acquire for yourself a friend" — that is, through the holy books written with a reed [kaneh] — bind them — [bind them] — to yourself and study them well. And through this you will be able to know who is the true teacher.

segments.he:
ד.
אין לך דבר שעומד בפני התשובה, ואפלו על פגם טפי המח, שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה שאין מועיל תשובה, כנזכר לעיל, וכן על אלו שמבאר במקרא: כל באיה לא ישובון ולא ישיגו ארחות חיים, אבל באמת לאמתו מועיל תשובה לכל החטאים, כמו שמצינו כבר כמה וכמה רשעים, שפגמו בטפי המח וכפרו בעקר ואף על פי כן נתקבלו נתקבלו בתשובה. רק מחמת שפגמו כל כך, על כן צריכין להצטרף ולהתנסות ולעמד בנסיון הזה של ההתרחקות הזאת, דהינו שכותבין עליו שאין מועיל תשובה, וכשהוא פתי וסכל ואינו מרחם על עצמו שלא לאבד את עולמו, חס ושלום, אזי מוצא פטור לעצמו להתרחק מן התשובה, מאחר שכבר נכתב עליו שאין מועיל לו תשובה, חס ושלום אבל מי שחושב באמת על תכליתו, ויש לו רחמנות על עצמו ומחשב את דרכיו, כי אוף על פי כן מה יהא בסופו ומה יעשה ליום פקודה, אזי כל מה שמוצא ורואה שמרחקין אותו יותר, הוא מרחם על עצמו יותר וצועק אל השם יתברך ויותר מעמקא דלבא, עד ישקיף וירא השם מן השמים, כי אף על פי שכבר נכתב עליו שאינו מתקבל בתשובה, אוף על פי כן צועק אל השם יתברך על זה בעצמו, שפגם כל כך עד שמרחקין אותו כל כך, ואף על פי שאני יודע שראוי להרחיקני מגדל הפגמים שלי, ובודאי כל מה שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה, הכל אמת ויציב, אוף על פי כן אני יודע ומאמין, שיש חסדי השם יתברך, ורחמים גדולים גדולים כאלו אצל השם יתברך, עד שיכול לקרבנו גם כן ברחמים ולקבלנו בתשובה שלמה, כי אוף על פי כן הלא אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה בעצמן: אין לך דבר שעומד בפני התשובה, ואזי כשזוכה לעמד בנסיון הזה של ההתרחקות כל כך ואף על פי כן שב בתשובה שלמה, אזי השם יתברך מרחם עליו ונתקרב על ידי זה דיקא, על ידי שעמד בנסיון הזה של ההתרחקות, וזה בחינת: התרחקות - תכלית ההתקרבות. (שם, הלכה ד', אות ד):
segments.en:
4.
There is nothing that stands before teshuvah. And even for the blemish of drops of the brain [tipei hamoi'ach] — about which our Sages of blessed memory said that teshuvah is not effective, as mentioned above — and likewise for those about whom the verse says: "All who come to her do not return, and they will not attain the paths of life" — but in truth, truth is truth: teshuvah is effective for all sins. As we have already found many, many wicked people who blemished in drops of the brain, and denied the very foundation — and even so they were accepted — [accepted] — in teshuvah.

Only — since they blemished so greatly — therefore they must be refined and tested and stand in this trial of the distancing. That is, it is written of them that teshuvah is not effective for them. And when a person is foolish and senseless and has no compassion upon himself — not to destroy his world, G-d forbid — then he finds an excuse and exemption for himself to distance himself from teshuvah. Since it has already been written of him that teshuvah is not effective for him, G-d forbid. But one who thinks in truth about his purpose — and has compassion upon himself and considers his ways — for even so what will become of him in the end, and what will he do on the day of reckoning? Then — the more he finds and sees that they distance him further — the more compassion he has upon himself and he cries out to G-d (blessed be He) from ever deeper in the depths of the heart. Until G-d looks down and sees from Heaven. For even though it has already been written of him that he is not accepted in teshuvah — even so he cries out to G-d (blessed be He) about this itself: that he has blemished so greatly that they distance him so greatly. And even though I know that it is fitting to distance me because of the greatness of my blemishes — and certainly all that our Sages of blessed memory said is true and firm — even so, I know and believe that there are kindnesses of G-d (blessed be He), and such great — [great] — compassion before G-d (blessed be He), that He can also draw us close with compassion and receive us in complete teshuvah. For even so, did our Sages of blessed memory not say themselves: "There is nothing that stands before teshuvah."

And then — when one merits to stand in this trial of the distancing, and even so returns in complete teshuvah — then G-d (blessed be He) has compassion upon him and he draws close through this specifically — through having stood in this trial of the distancing. And this is the aspect of: the distancing is the ultimate drawing close.

(ibid., Halacha 4, item 4).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for they are dwellers of the dust [shochnei ofor]. Who even in their lifetimes made themselves neighbors to dust — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And through this they have the aspect of the drawing power that dust has — that is, they have the power to draw toward themselves the holiness of His blessed G-dliness and to draw the entire world toward the holiness of His blessed service. And how much more so now — after the passing — when they are literally dwellers of the dust. And then at the place of the burial of the Tzadik — the dust there is in the aspect of the dust of the Land of Israel — holy soil [admas kodesh]. In the aspect of: "the righteous shall inherit the land" [Psalms 37:29] — as explained elsewhere. And therefore it is easy to truly awaken there to His blessed service — and to strengthen the drawing power of holiness over the compelling power.

segments.he:
ה.
עקר כל הפגמים של כל החטאים הם בבחינת העשרים ושתים אתון, שממשיך חס ושלום האותיות, שיש באותו הדבר שעובר עליו, למקום שממשיך להסטרא אחרא וכו', רחמנא לצלן, כי עקר החיות של כל הדברים הם האותיות שיש בהם, כידוע, ועל כן עקר התקון - על ידי הדבור בבחינת: קחו עמכם דברים ושובו אל השם, ואמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: אינו מבקש מכם אלא דברים, הינו שירבה לדבר דבורים קדושים של צעקות ותחנות ובקשות ושירות ותשבחות אליו יתברך, עד שיצטרפו ויתקנו כל האותיות לטוב, ובודאי הוא עצה גדולה וקלה, שהכל יכולין לקימה, כי יכולין לזכות לתשובה ולחיי העולם הבא על ידי הדבור לבד, אף על פי שאינו זוכה להתיגע ולטרח בעבודתו כמו הצדיקים והכשרים שהיו לפנינו, שיגעו וטרחו מאד מאד בתעניתים רבים ובסגופים קשים ועצומים מאד ואפלו אם, חס ושלום, עדין עובר עליו מה שעובר, אוף על פי כן אם לא יניח את עצמו לפל לעולם ויחזק את עצמו לדבר דבורים על כל פנים תמיד לפני השם יתברך בצעקות ותחנות ובקשות הרבה להשם יתברך, בודאי סוף כל סוף ישוב להשם יתברך אך הבעל דבר מתגבר על האדם למנעו למנעו גם מזה, והעקר על ידי טרדת הפרנסה, שעל ידי זה אינו עוסק בשלמות אפלו בעצה קלה הזאת לשוב להשם יתברך על ידי הדבור הקדוש על כן צריכין להזכיר את עצמו בכל פעם האמת, כי לא בכח יגבר איש, ואין הפרנסה נמשכת נמשכת על ידי יגיעתו וטרחו לבד, רק הכל בחסדי השם ובישועתו, והדאגות והטרדות אינם מועילים כלל לפרנסה, אדרבא, מזיקים הרבה לפרנסה, ועל כן אפלו הבעל מלאכה ועסק יכול למצא לנפשו כמה שעות ביום לעסק בהם באמירת תהלים והתבודדות וכו', ועל ידי זה ישוב בודאי להשם יתברך לחיי העולם הבא. (הלכות קריאת שמע, הלכה ה', אות יד):
segments.en:
5.
The essential of all the blemishes of all the sins is in the aspect of the twenty-two letters. For one draws, G-d forbid, the letters that are in that matter in which he transgresses — to a place that draws them toward the sitra achra, etc., G-d protect us. For the essential vitality of all things is the letters within them — as is known. And therefore the essential repair is through speech — in the aspect of: "Take with you words and return to G-d". And our Sages of blessed memory said: "He asks of you nothing but words." That is, one should multiply speaking holy words of cries and supplications and requests and songs and praises to Him, blessed be He. Until all the letters will be joined and repaired for good. And certainly this is a great and easy counsel — that everyone can fulfill. For one can merit teshuvah and the life of the World to Come through speech alone. Even if one does not merit to toil and labor in his service like the Tzaddikim and the upright who preceded us — who toiled and labored very, very greatly in many fasts and harsh and enormous mortifications. And even if, G-d forbid, what passes over him still passes over him — even so, if he does not allow himself to ever fall — and strengthens himself to speak words at the very least always before G-d (blessed be He) — with cries and many supplications and requests to G-d (blessed be He) — certainly in the end he will return to G-d (blessed be He).

But the baal davar intensifies against a person to prevent him — [to prevent him] — even from this. And the essential [obstruction] is through the entanglement of livelihood — through which one does not engage fully even in this easy counsel to return to G-d (blessed be He) through holy speech. And therefore one must remind himself every single time of the truth — that "it is not through strength that a man prevails". And livelihood does not derive — [derive] — through one's toil and labor alone — but everything comes through the kindness of G-d and His salvation. And worries and entanglements do not help at all for livelihood — on the contrary, they damage livelihood greatly. And therefore even a craftsman or businessman can find himself some hours in the day to engage in the recitation of Psalms and hisbodidus, etc. And through this he will certainly return to G-d (blessed be He) for the life of the World to Come.

(Hilchos Kriyas Shma, Halacha 5, item 14).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The great virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for there everyone can be repaired. Even one who is between two [forces of the] adversary, G-d forbid — the great Tzadik can extract him from there — when one comes to his holy grave and wishes to return in complete teshuvah. For the death of the great Tzadik is very high and elevated and exalted. And then specifically he intensifies with all his strength to complete what he needs to complete for the benefit of the souls of Israel. For the death of the Tzadik is the aspect of prayer in the aspect of judgment [b'ves din] — for the great ba'al ko'ach [master of power] prays — and the sitra achra swallows it. And the prayer — since it is very holy and came from a great ba'al ko'ach — the sitra achra does not have the power to swallow it entirely. Rather, on the contrary — the prayer stands in its throat [b'tzavoroh] — until the sitra achra is compelled through this to vomit and expel and return all the holinesses it has swallowed — including the very essence of its vitality.

segments.he:
ו.
צריך כל אדם להשתדל מאד לבקש ולחפש אחר האבדות כל ימי חייו, כי זה כל האדם, שנברא רק בשביל זה - לבקש אחר אבדות, שהם בחינת ניצוצות הנפולין, שהם בחינת נאבדים ונדחים, שצריך כל אדם להשתדל מאד לבקש ולחפש אחריהם כל ימי חייו, ובפרט אם כבר חטא ופגם כפי מה שפגם, ובפרט פגם הברית, חס ושלום, שעל ידי זה חזר ואבד בעצמו אבדות הרבה, וצריך לחפש ולבקש מאד אחריהם, וכשיבקש ויחפש היטב, בודאי ימצא, כי: יגעתי ולא מצאתי - אל תאמין. וזה עקר התשובה על העוונות, כמו שכתוב: ושבת עד השם אלקיך וכו', אם יהיה נדחך בקצה השמים משם יקבצך וכו', וכתיב: ובקשתם משם את השם אלקיך ומצאת וכו', כי צריכין לבקש ולחפש מאד אחר דרכי הקדושה, כי כל מה שהאדם רחוק מהשם יתברך, הוא מחמת האבדות הנ"ל, שעל ידי זה הוא הולך ותועה כשה אובד, ואינו יכול למצא דרך החיים, ועל כן צריך האדם להשתדל מאד כל ימיו לבקש ולחפש אחר אבדותיו, כי זה עקר התשובה כנ"ל ואם יבקש ויחפש היטב, בודאי ימצא כל מה שצריך לתקון נפשו, ואפלו בעת שאינו זוכה למצא עדין, אוף על פי כן על ידי כל יגיעה וחפוש כבר מצא הרבה, כי אין שום יגיעה ובקשה נאבד כלל, ובודאי מצא כבר הרבה על ידי כל דבור ודבור ועל ידי כל יגיעה וחפוש, כי לית רעותא טבא דאתאבד, ואפלו אם אינו רואה כלל מה שמצא,, ונדמה לו, שעדין לא מצא כלום ועדין הוא רחוק מהשם יתברך כמקדם, אוף על פי כן צריכין להאמין באמונה שלמה, שבודאי מצא הרבה על ידי היגיעה בעצמה, כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה יגעתי ומצאתי - תאמין תאמין דיקא, אף על פי שעדין אין רואין מה שמצא. (הלכות ברכות הפרות, הלכה ה', אות א):
segments.en:
6.
Every person must strive greatly to seek and search after the lost things [avaidoas] all the days of his life. For this is the entire purpose of a person — who was created only for this: to seek after the lost things. Which are the aspect of the fallen sparks [nitzotzos hanefilim] — that are the aspect of things lost and cast away — that every person must strive greatly to seek and search after them all the days of his life. And especially if one has already sinned and blemished according to however he has blemished — especially the blemish of the bris, G-d forbid — through which he has now lost many more things himself. And one must search and seek after them greatly. And when one searches and seeks well — certainly he will find. For: "I toiled and did not find — do not believe".

And this is the essential teshuvah for sins — as it is written: "And you will return to G-d your G-d, etc. — even if your scattered ones are at the very end of the heavens — from there He will gather you, etc.". And it is written: "And you will seek from there G-d your G-d and you will find, etc.". For one must greatly seek and search after the paths of holiness. For all the distance a person is from G-d (blessed be He) is on account of the aforementioned lost things — through which he goes and wanders like a lost sheep and cannot find the path of life. And therefore a person must strive greatly all his days to seek and search after his lost things. For this is the essential teshuvah as above. And if one searches and seeks well — certainly he will find all that is needed for the repair of his soul. And even at the time when he does not yet merit to find — even so, through every toil and searching he has already found much. For no toil and searching is ever lost at all. And certainly one has already found much through every single word and through every toil and searching. For lais re'usa tava d'is'avad [no good intention is ever lost]. And even if one sees nothing of what he has found — and it appears to him that he has still not found anything and he is still far from G-d (blessed be He) as before — even so, one must believe with complete faith that certainly one has found much through the toil itself. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "I toiled and found — believe" — believe specifically. Even though one does not yet see what he found.

(Hilchos Bircas HaPeiros, Halacha 5, item 1).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And this is the secret of the repairs and extractions that were done until now through the death of the ten martyrs [asarah harugei malchus] — as is brought in the sacred writings. And in truth the death of all the Tzaddikim is the aspect of mesiras nefesh [self-sacrifice] for the sanctification of G-d's Name. Especially the death of the Tzaddikim in the diaspora — where all of this is in the manner of the prayer in the aspect of judgment. For they surrender their body to be buried in the diaspora — where the dominion of the sitra achra resides. And it seems to the sitra achra that it is swallowing this holy body. But this holy body is a great ba'al ko'ach and stands in the sitra achra's throat — until it is compelled through this to vomit greatly from within itself and from its belly — until the Tzadik completes what he began. For even during his lifetime he engaged in this all his days and gave his soul for this. And after his passing, he does not stop engaging in this holy service — until everything is completed for the good as he wishes.

segments.he:
ז.
עקר התשובה של כל אדם הוא, שישוב בכל פעם מהמחשבות רעות שנלכד בהם למחשבות קדושות בבחינת: יעזב רשע דרכו ואיש און מחשבתיו וישב אל השם. וזה עקר התשובה, לשוב במחשבתו ממקום שהוא שם למחשבות קדושות, ואפלו אם נתעה במחשבתו כמו שנתעה, אוף על פי כן צריך שיאמין, שבכל מה שמנתק עצמו במחשבתו מרע לטוב הוא יקר בעיני השם, כי הוא ידע יצרנו וכו', ועקר היצר הרע הם המחשבות, כמבאר בפנים. (הלכות תפלת המנחה, הלכה ז', אות ב, צא):
segments.en:
7.
The essential teshuvah of every person is to return every single time from the evil thoughts in which he has been caught — to holy thoughts. In the aspect of: "Let the wicked abandon his way, and the man of iniquity his thoughts, and let him return to G-d". And this is the essential teshuvah: to return in one's thought from wherever one is — to holy thoughts. And even if one has gone astray in his thought however he has gone astray — even so, one must believe that in every way he disconnects himself in his thought from bad to good — it is precious in the eyes of G-d. For "He knows our formation, etc.". And the essential yetzer hara is the thoughts — as explained in the inner teachings.

(Hilchos Tefillas HaMinchah, Halacha 7, items 2, 91).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore there — upon his holy grave — every person can be repaired. Even the worst of the worst. If he merits to come there during his lifetime and to request and pray there for the repair of his soul. And this too is the matter of the ten Psalms chapters ordained to be said there — see the inner teachings.

segments.he:
ח.
ענין מה שמבאר בזהר הקדוש, שעל פגם הברית אין מועיל תשובה, ואף על פי כן מבאר בספרים שגם על זה מועיל תשובה, אך עקר תשובתו, שישליך שכל עצמו לגמרי ויתחזק באמונה שלמה וכו'. (הלכות נדה, הלכה ב', אות יא):
segments.en:
8.
The matter of what is explained in the holy Zohar — that for the blemish of the bris, teshuvah is not effective. And yet it is explained in the sacred books that even for this teshuvah is effective. But his essential repentance is: to cast aside one's own understanding entirely and to strengthen oneself in complete faith, etc.

(Hilchos Niddah, Halacha 2, item 11).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Through meriting to support the Tzadik [financially] — through this it is easier to receive from him the illumination of his holy da'as. Until one can merit through this to eat himself also in great holiness and to receive the illumination of will at the time of eating. Also through this — [through this] — one can receive extra illumination from the remaining da'as [hashoras hada'as] left by the Tzadik — even after his passing.

segments.he:
ט.
עקר כל הפגמים והחטאים, רחמנא לצלן, נמשכין מבחינת גזל, הינו ממה שהאדם דוחק את השעה, שזה בחינת גזל, כמבאר בפנים, כי אין היצר הרע מצוי אלא לשעתו, ואם יעמד בנסיון בשעה קלה, אזי אחר כך ממילא יתבטל וילך ממנו היצר הרע, על כן עקר תקון התשובה נמשך על ידי הצדיקים הגדולים, שאינם דוחקים את השעה כלל, אפלו בתפלתם, ומתפללים רק ברחמים ותחנונים. גם הצדיקים האלו אינם משתמשים עם המטה עז שלהם, כי אם בשביל להכניע הרע שבעדה, ועל ידי זה זוכין ישראל לתשובה. גם כי עקר ההתרחקות מתשובה הוא על ידי בני אדם המונעים, כי בני אדם הם לפעמים מונעים גדולים מאד יותר מהיצר הרע, הינו על ידי מחלקת והליצנות שלהם וכיוצא, כמבאר בפנים, ועל כן על ידי הצדיקי אמת, שממשיכין חדושי תורתם בשלמות כל התקונים, עד שעל ידי זה מקבלין כח להעניש את המונעים או להשתיק אותם על כל פנים, על ידי זה נמשך התעוררות התשובה בעולם. (הלכות גזלה, הלכה ה', אות יז):
segments.en:
9.
The essential of all blemishes and sins, G-d protect us, derives from the aspect of theft [gezail] — that is, from the fact that a person presses the moment [dochek es hasha'ah]. Which is the aspect of theft — as explained in the inner teachings. For the yetzer hara is only present for its hour. And if a person stands firm in the trial for a small amount of time — then afterwards the yetzer hara is automatically nullified and departs from him. And therefore the essential repair of teshuvah is drawn through the great Tzaddikim who press the moment not at all — even in their prayer. And they pray only with compassion and supplication. Also these Tzaddikim do not use their powerful staff [mateh az] — except for the sake of subduing the evil within the congregation [edah]. And through this Israel merits teshuvah. Also because the essential distancing from teshuvah is through people who obstruct [mone'im]. For people are sometimes very great obstructors — more than the yetzer hara itself. That is, through their controversy and their mockery and the like — as explained in the inner teachings. And therefore through the truly righteous Tzaddikim who draw their Torah innovations in completeness of all the repairs — through this they receive power to punish the obstructors or at least to silence them. Through this the awakening of teshuvah is drawn in the world.

(Hilchos Gezailah, Halacha 5, item 17).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Also one can receive through this [supporting the Tzadik] an abundant flow of blessing and great wealth.

segments.he:
י.
יש שפגם וחטא כל כך, עד שהוא בבחינת גזל את הרבים, שהפגמים שלו נוגעים לכלל ישראל, חס ושלום, ואזי כל תקונו - לעסק בצרכי רבים, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: גזל את הרבים - יעשה מהן צרכי רבים, ועקר צרכי רבים הוא לזכותם לתכלית הנצחי, והעקר להשתדל שיהיה לו חלק בהמשכת חדושי תורתם של הצדיקי אמת, שנמשכו בשלמות כל התקונים, עד שעל ידם עקר המשכת תקון התשובה לכל ישראל כנ"ל, וצריכים להשתדל מאד שיתפשטו בעולם, הן על ידי שיסיע בממונו להעוסקים בזה, הן בגופו, הן בשאר הבחינות, כי כל אחד יכול לזכות שיהיה לו חלק בזה, ועל ידי זה יזכה את הרבים בחינת צרכי רבים, וזהו עקר התקון לכל הפגמים שלו, שהם בחינת גוזל את הרבים כנ"ל. (שם, אות יח):
segments.en:
10.
There is one who has blemished and sinned so greatly — until he is in the aspect of one who has robbed the multitude [gazal es harabbim]. Whose blemishes affect all of Israel, G-d forbid. And then his entire repair is to engage in the needs of the multitude [tzorchei rabbim] — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "One who robbed the multitude — let him do from it the needs of the multitude." And the essential needs of the multitude are to cause them to merit the eternal purpose. And the essential [means] is to strive to have a share in drawing the Torah innovations of the truly righteous Tzaddikim — which were drawn forth with all the repairs complete. Through which the essential drawing of the repair of teshuvah for all of Israel comes — as above. And one must strive greatly that they spread in the world — whether through supporting with money those who engage in this, whether in person, whether through other aspects. For every single person can merit to have a share in this. And through this he will cause the multitude to merit — in the aspect of the needs of the multitude. And this is the essential repair for all his blemishes — which are the aspect of one who robbed the multitude as above.

(ibid., item 18).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Through the journey and travel that each person makes from his place to the Tzadik — through this he elevates his place to the aspect of mekomo shel olam [the place of the world] — which is the Tzadik. And this is the aspect of what people journey and travel to the graves of the Tzaddikim — especially before Rosh Hashanah. For in the place where the Tzadik lies — that is the place of his rest — in the aspect of: "they will come to peace; they will rest upon their resting places" [Isaiah 57:2]. And the essential rest of the Tzadik is when he is bound and encompassed in the aspect of the Throne of Glory — the aspect of mekomo shel olam — where the essential rest and the inheritance reside — in the aspect of: "And a glorious throne shall He cause them to inherit, etc." [I Samuel 2:8]. And therefore there — in the place of the Tzadik's resting — every person merits that he will be judged mercifully from Above — and be judged to the scale of merit — through the aspect of mekomo shel olam.

segments.he:
יא.
מה שמובא בזהר הקדוש, שעל פגם הברית אין מועיל תשובה, אך אוף על פי כן על ידי אמונת חכמים בשלמות יוכל להתקן גם עון זה בכח התורה הקדושה, שממשכת המתקה מבחינת חכמה עלאה. (הלכות פריה ורביה, הלכה א, אות י):
segments.en:
11.
What is brought in the holy Zohar — that for the blemish of the bris, teshuvah is not effective — but even so, through complete faith in the sages, even this sin can be repaired through the power of the holy Torah, which draws sweetening from the aspect of the supernal wisdom [chochmah ila'ah].

(Hilchos Priyah u'Riviyah, Halacha 1, item 10).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Every time one weeps over the passing of the Tzadik and searches and seeks after him as is proper — then one draws out his holiness through the son or the disciple who fills the place of his father and master. For this is a great principle: the Tzadik does not depart from the world until another is born in his place. As our Sages of blessed memory said [on the verse]: "The sun also rises and the sun also sets, etc." [Ecclesiastes 1:5]. But one must seek and search after this very much — [very much] — especially in these generations.

segments.he: ערך תמימות
segments.en: Wholeness and Simplicity

origin.notice: Editorial English rendering of the supplied Hebrew heading or closing text.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And therefore even though one must weep and mourn greatly over the passing of the Tzadik — even so, one must be very careful not to stumble through this and say that the Tzadik has already died and there is no more hope, G-d forbid, and that no successor or remnant of him remains in the world. For this is a very great blemish. For certainly the Tzadik has not died — and certainly the remnant [hashoras] of his holiness remains with his sons and his disciples. Only one must search and seek after this very — [very] — greatly. And through every search and seeking, one certainly finds the holiness of his remnant with his sons and disciples. Which is the aspect of: "There Aaron died, and Elazar his son served as priest in his place" [Deuteronomy 10:6] — as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he:
א.
כשרואה אדם, שיש לו עקמימות בלבו, בפרט כשיש לו, חס ושלום, עקמימות הרבה בלבו, אזי הוא צריך לשום עצמו כבהמה ולסלק דעתו לגמרי כאלו אין לו שום דעת כלל ולסמך רק על אמונה וילך רק בתמימות ובפשיטות לבד, ואזי זוכה אחר כך לדעת גדול מאד בחינת מחין של תפלין. (הלכות תפלין, הלכה ד', אות ו):
segments.en:
1.
When a person sees that he has crookedness in his heart — especially when he has, G-d forbid, much crookedness in his heart — then he must make himself like an animal and set aside his mind entirely — as if he has no mind at all. And rely only on faith. And go only in temimus [wholeness] and peshitus [simplicity] alone. And then he merits afterwards to very great da'as — the aspect of the expanded consciousness [moichin] of tefillin.

(Hilchos Tefillin, Halacha 4, item 6).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: It is the way of many people to say after the passing of the Tzadik, G-d forbid: "Now we have nothing left at all, G-d forbid." And even though from one side they speak some truth — for certainly there has not remained literally a Tzadik exactly like him. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "The face of Moshe is like the face of the sun; the face of Yehoshua is like the face of the moon. Woe for that shame, etc." — even so, even so, it is forbidden to remain, G-d forbid, with this and to say that therefore all hope is lost, G-d forbid. For the opposite is the case — for G-d will never abandon His people. And "Your dominion is in every generation" [Psalms 145:13]. Therefore one must believe that even though one must certainly pine very greatly after the true Tzadik in the aspect of Moshe — even so, one must conclude with words of comfort — to comfort and gladden oneself in his remnant: that is, the holy innovations of Torah that remain from him through his books and his disciples. For from a truly righteous Tzadik, certainly a good remnant remains forever. Only one must search and seek much as above.

segments.he:
ב.
כל העקמימות שיש בלב הרבה בני אדם, שאומרים, שאינם יכולים לעסק בעבודת השם מחמת חסרון פרנסה ושאר יסורין ומניעות, חס ושלום, כל זה נמשך מבחינת המבוכה של הקושיא של צדיק ורע לו רשע וטוב לו, שזאת המבוכה מבלבל הרבה בני אדם, ואפלו מי שאינו נכנס כלל במחשבתו בקושיא זאת, אוף על פי כן כל כל הדבורים הנ"ל, הכל נמשך ונשתלשל משם, ועקר התקון לזה הוא רק תמימות ופשיטות, להשליך כל החכמות ולבלי להרהר אחריו יתברך כלל ולידע ולהאמין ולהאמין כי ישרים דרכי השם ולהתגבר בכל מה שעובר עליו לחטף בכל יום איזה טוב כל מה שיוכל, כי לית יום דלית בה טוב, ולא יהרהר על משפטיו יתברך כלל, שזה עקר האמונה - להאמין שהכל מהשם יתברך ואין להרהר אחריו כלל, כי צדיק וישר הוא, ובזה בעצמו ממתיקין הדינים וזוכין להתקרב להתקרב להשם יתברך דיקא על ידי כל זה שעובר עליו. (הלכות ראש חדש, הלכה ו', אות יב):
segments.en:
2.
All the crookedness in the heart of many people — who say that they are unable to engage in the service of G-d because of deficiency of livelihood and other sufferings and obstacles, G-d forbid — all of this derives from the aspect of the confusion of the question of tzadik v'ra lo, rasha v'tov lo [why the righteous suffer and the wicked prosper]. For this confusion confuses many people. And even one who does not enter this question into his thought at all — even so, all of — [all of] — the aforementioned words derive and flow from there. And the essential repair for this is only temimus and simplicity: to cast aside all the wisdoms — and not to question His ways at all, blessed be He. And to know and believe — and believe — that "the ways of G-d are straight". And to overpower oneself in all that passes over him — to seize some good each day — as much as possible. For lais yoma d'lais bei tava [there is no day that does not have good in it]. And to not question His blessed judgments at all. For this is the essential faith: to believe that everything is from G-d (blessed be He) — and not to question Him at all. For He is righteous and upright. And through this itself one sweetens the judgments. And merits to draw close — [to draw close] — to G-d (blessed be He) specifically through all that passes over him.

(Hilchos Rosh Chodesh, Halacha 6, item 12).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: Certainly G-d can sustain the poor and give them all good directly. But the essential commandment of tzedakah is because the money is already in the wealthy person's hand — and it is in his power to do with it as he wishes. And he overpowers [his inclination] through his free will and gives from his own pocket to tzedakah. This is very precious before G-d. For through this he draws chassadim [kindnesses] into the world. And this is His blessed will — that the human being who has free will draw [kindnesses] into the world through the tzedakah he gives to the poor of his own free will. And in all of this we see the greatness of the power of free will.

segments.he:
ג.
צריך כל אחד להסתכל בנפשו, שלא יצא מדרכי התמימות באמת, ולחפש דרכיו בכל עת, ולשמר נפשו מאד, שלא יטה אותו הבעל דבר מן האמת, חס ושלום, על ידי חכמות של הבל, המצויים עתה בעוונותינו הרבים, ושלא יהפך לו אמת לשקר ועברה למצוה, חס ושלום, כי זה גרוע מן הכל, חס ושלום, ויזכר את עצמו בכל עת איך שאינו נקי בענין תאות משגל, ועל ידי זה כלי כלי המחין שלו אינם בשלמות, ואפלו אם הוא מוחזק ומפורסם ללמדן גדול וחסיד, אוף על פי כן מאחר שיודע בנפשו, שאינו נקי וזך בענין זה בשלמות כראוי, וממילא תפיסת המחין שלו אינם בשלמות, על כן תכף כשרוצה הבעל דבר להטותו מדרך התמימות האמתי אפלו נקודה בעלמא, ואף על פי שנדמה לו שעל פי התורה מגיע כך, צריך לירא לנפשו ולחשב אולי אולי טועה הוא בדבר ומחשבה זו וסברא זאת נמשך אצלו מבחינת: לא זכה - נעשית לו סם מות, רחמנא לצלן, שנאמר על מי שלא זכה עדין לשלמות כלי המחין על ידי תקון הברית בשלמות, על כן הוא הוא צריך לזהר ביותר שלא להטעות את עצמו ושלא להפך דברי אלקים חיים, חס ושלום, וביותר ויותר צריך לזהר בענין זה לענין מחלקת, כאשר כבר ראינו כמה נפשות שירדו חיים שאולה, רחמנא לצלן, על ידי שהרבו במחלקת על הכשרים מחמת טעות דעתם ושנדמה להם כאלו כונתם לשם שמים, וכמבאר בפנים. וגם לענין עצמו לבד בעבודת השם, צריכין גם כן לצעק ולזעק הרבה להשם יתברך, שיוליכהו בדרך הישר והאמת תמיד, אולי יזכה להתקרב להשם יתברך כראוי, וכאשר צעק דוד המלך הרבה על זה, כמבאר בפנים, כי צריכין לזכות גדול וישועה גדולה ורחמים גדולים והשתדלות ויגיעה גדולה כל ימי חייו, שיזכה לפלס דרכיו באמת בכל עת ולילך בדרך הקדש באמת לאמתו ולא יטה לימין ולשמאל ולא יטעה את עצמו באיזה דבר, חס ושלום, על ידי שאין הכלים של המחין שלו שלמים כראוי, אבל על כל פנים כששומר את עצמו שלא יהיה נוטה על כל פנים מדרכי התמימות, אזי הוא בטוח על כל פנים ממכשול גמור, חס ושלום, כי הולך בתם ילך בטח. (הלכות יין נסך, הלכה ד', אות יג, טז, יז):
segments.en:
3.
Every person must look into his own soul — that he not depart from the ways of true temimus. And to search his ways at all times. And to guard his soul very much — that the baal davar should not divert him from the truth, G-d forbid, through the futile wisdoms that are so common now in our many sins. And that he not invert truth to falsehood and transgression to commandment for him, G-d forbid. For this is the worst of all, G-d forbid. And he should remind himself at all times — that he is not pure in the matter of the desire for sexual union. And through this — the vessels — [the vessels] — of his brain are not in perfection. And even if he is established and known as a great scholar and pious person — even so, since he knows within his own soul that he is not pure and clear in this matter in full perfection as is proper — and therefore his grasp of the mind is not in perfection — therefore immediately when the baal davar wishes to divert him from the path of true temimus even by a single point — even though it seems to him that the Torah mandates such — he must fear for his soul and consider: perhaps — [perhaps] — he is erring in the matter. And this thought and view derives in him from the aspect of: "if he has not merited — it becomes for him a deadly poison", G-d protect us — said of one who has not yet merited the perfection of the vessels of the brain through the repair of the bris in perfection. Therefore — he — [he] — must be especially careful not to mislead himself and not to invert the words of the living G-d, G-d forbid.

And he must be especially, especially careful in this matter regarding controversy. As we have already seen many souls who went down to the pit alive, G-d protect us, through having multiplied controversy against the upright because of the error of their mind — and it seemed to them that their intention was for the sake of Heaven. As is explained in the inner teachings. And also for himself alone in the service of G-d — one must also cry out and wail greatly to G-d (blessed be He), that He lead him in the straight and true path always. Perhaps he will merit to draw close to G-d (blessed be He) as is proper. And as King David cried out much about this — as explained in the inner teachings. For one needs great merit and great salvation and great compassion — and great striving and great toil all the days of his life — to merit to weigh out his ways in truth at every time and to walk in the holy path truly and truthfully and not deviate right or left. And not to mislead himself in any matter, G-d forbid — on account of the imperfection of the vessels of his brain. But at the very least — when one guards himself from deviating at the very least from the ways of temimus — then he is at least certainly protected from utter stumbling, G-d forbid. For "he who walks in wholeness walks securely".

(Hilchos Yayin Nesech, Halacha 4, items 13, 16, 17).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The repair of all wayfarers — physically and spiritually — is through tzedakah. For the essential knowledge of the truly straight path in its true truth — it is impossible to instruct explicitly, but only through a hint — in the aspect of: "I will instruct you and show you the way you should go — I will counsel you with My eye upon you" [Psalms 32:8]. For it is impossible to explain all the confusions and errors that arise in traveling the paths — even in the physical. How much more so in the matter of spiritual paths and trails in the service of G-d — where it is certainly impossible to explain and specify for each and every person the straight path at every day and every time, as to where to turn to rescue his soul from what needs to be rescued — except through a hint. That a hint is given to a person at every time: "in this way go." And all of this is repaired through tzedakah — in the aspect of: "the righteousness of the wholesome straightens his way" [Proverbs 11:5]. For through tzedakah one merits to walk in the straight path — physically and spiritually.

segments.he:
ד.
כל מי שמרגיש בעצמו, שאינו קדוש כראוי, צריך להכניע ולבטל עצמו נגד השם יתברך ולא ירצה לילך בגדולות ובנפלאות ממנו להמשיך על עצמו בחינת רוח הקדש, רוח נבואה, מאחר שיודע שרחוק מזה, ואם ירצה להמשיך על עצמו בחינת מראות וחזיונות, יוכל לקלקל יותר ויותר, כאשר נכשלו בזה רבים מאד, רק צריך שילך בתמימות ולבקש מהשם יתברך, שיהיה בעזרו לצאת מפחיתותו ויזכה לקדש את עצמו כראוי, ואז - אם יזכה ויהיה ראוי לזה לקבל רוח הקדש, דרך הקדושה, בשלמות - השם הטוב יעשה עמו כרצונו. (הלכות חדש, הלכה ד', אות ח):
segments.en:
4.
Every person who feels in himself that he is not holy as is proper — must humble and nullify himself before G-d (blessed be He). And not wish to go in matters too great and too wondrous for him [gedolos u'niflo'os mimenu] — to draw upon himself the aspect of the holy spirit, the spirit of prophecy. Since he knows that he is far from this. And if he wishes to draw upon himself the aspect of visions and sights — he can cause himself even more and more ruin. As very many have stumbled in this. Rather, he must go in temimus and beseech G-d (blessed be He) to be in his aid — to emerge from his insignificance. And to merit to sanctify himself as is proper. And then — if he merits and is worthy of receiving the holy spirit, through the path of holiness, in perfection — G-d who is good will do with him as He wills.

(Hilchos Chadash, Halacha 4, item 8).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: The virtue of the commandment of tzedakah is without measure — and all the Torah and all the repair of the worlds depends upon this. For everything was created for His honor — and all His honor is revealed through tzedakah. Through which [the world] becomes a vessel to receive the flow of the supernal delight [no'am ha'elyon] — through which birth [holadah] occurs and His honor is revealed. As explained in the inner teachings. And therefore tzedakah is equivalent to the entire Torah — as our Sages of blessed memory said.

segments.he:
ה.
באמת אין לך אדם שאין לו שעה, אך הרבה אובדים השעה שלהם, שהיה יכול להצליח בה בגשמיות וברוחניות, על ידי חכמתם של הבל, על ידי שדוחקים את השעה, כמו שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה: כל הדוחק את השעה, השעה דוחקתו, כי השם יתברך מקים: עם גבר תמים תתמם ועם עקש תתפתל, ומאחר שהוא עקש ורוצה שימלא לו השם יתברך תכף חפצו, וכשאין לו מה שחפץ הוא אומר, שאי אפשר בזה האפן לעבד את השם יתברך נמצא, שהוא עקש ומהרהר אחר מדותיו יתברך, ואז גם השם יתברך מתפתל עמו והשעה דוחקתו אבל ההולך בתמימות ומאמין באמת כי בודאי צדיק וישר השם, ומה שסובל יסורין ודחקות - הכל לטובה, כי עדין לא הגיעה השעה שלו, ומקים: טוב ויחיל ודומם לתשועת השם, כי לפעמים אין השם יתברך נותן להאדם צרכי ישועתו תכף, עד שירבה בתפלה על זה, כי השם יתברך מתאוה לתפלתן של ישראל], וגם בתפלה אסור לדחק את השעה, כמבאר במקום אחר, ולפעמים הישועה מתעכבת עוד מטעמים אחרים, על כן צריכין לילך רק בתמימות ולהאמין בישר משפטיו יתברך ולהרבות בתפלה תמיד על כל דבר, ואז בודאי השעה עומדת לו, כי בודאי תגיע השעה של ישועתו. וכן מבאר בדברי חכמינו זכרונם לברכה: כל המתמים עצמו, שעה עומדת לו וכו'. (הלכות נזיקין, הלכה ה', אות טו):
segments.en:
5.
In truth there is no person who does not have his hour [sha'ah]. But many lose their hour — in which they could have succeeded physically and spiritually — through their futile wisdoms. Through pressing the moment [dochek es hasha'ah]. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "Whoever presses the moment — the moment presses him." For G-d (blessed be He) fulfills: "with the wholesome You act wholesomely, and with the crooked You act crookedly". And since he is crooked and wishes G-d (blessed be He) to immediately fulfill his desire — and when he does not have what he desires, he says that it is impossible in this way to serve G-d (blessed be He) — it is thus found that he is crooked and deliberates regarding His blessed attributes. And then G-d (blessed be He) also acts crookedly with him — and the moment presses him.

But one who goes in temimus and truly believes that G-d is certainly righteous and upright — and that the sufferings and hardship he endures are all for the good — for his hour has not yet come. And fulfills: "It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of G-d". For sometimes G-d (blessed be He) does not give the person the needs of his salvation immediately — until he multiplies prayer about this. For "G-d (blessed be He) longs for the prayer of Israel." And also in prayer it is forbidden to press the moment — as explained elsewhere. And sometimes the salvation is delayed still for other reasons. And therefore one must go only in temimus — and believe in the uprightness of His blessed judgments — and always multiply prayer for everything. And then certainly the moment stands [favorably] for him. For certainly the hour of his salvation will come. And as is explained in the words of our Sages of blessed memory: "Whoever makes himself whole [mistemim] — the moment stands favorably for him, etc."

(Hilchos Nezikkin, Halacha 5, item 15).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: But one must give much tzedakah — and request from G-d that he merit to fulfill the commandment of tzedakah as is proper: that he give the tzedakah with a full heart for the sake of His Name, truly. And that G-d send him worthy poor people through whom to merit. For the essential repair of tzedakah is that through it His honor should be magnified as above. And therefore one must intend in his charity only for the honor of G-d — not for his own honor, G-d forbid. Not as is found with many people who give tzedakah only to those who have dominion and prestige in the world — and therefore the tzedakah is also for their honor. And upon the worthy and upright poor who engage in Torah and the service of G-d in truth — they pay no attention to them at all and avert their eyes from them. It is thus found that the tzedakah they give is only for their own honor.

segments.he:
ו.
מי שהולך בתמימות, הוא עקר הבן החביב להשם יתברך, כמבאר בפנים, ומי שהולך אחר החכמות והערמימיות של הבל, שהם כמו בחינת נחושים ממש, רחמנא לצלן, הוא בחינת עקש ופתלתל, והשם יתברך מקים עמו: עם עקש תתפתל, והוא בחינת בעל מום, שהוא ההפך מתמימות, שהוא לשון שלמות. (שם, אות טז):
segments.en:
6.
One who goes in temimus — he is the essential beloved child before G-d (blessed be He), as explained in the inner teachings. And one who goes after the futile wisdoms and cunning schemes [armimiyos] of vanity — which are like actual divinations [nachushim mamash], G-d protect us — he is the aspect of crooked and twisted [ikaish u'fsaltal]. And G-d (blessed be He) fulfills with him: "with the crooked You act crookedly". And he is the aspect of one with a blemish [ba'al mum] — which is the opposite of wholeness [temimus] — which is the language of completeness [shleimus].

(ibid., item 16).

origin.notice: English based on the supplied translation witness, incorporating source-bound corrections where needed.

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: And even though certainly even in such tzedakah there are good points — but through tzedakah such as this, the aforementioned vessel is not made in perfection to receive through it the flow of the supernal delight in perfection. And therefore the essential repair of tzedakah is that it should be in the aspect of a minchah [meal-offering] — which is the sacrifice of the poor person, whose giving is small. And therefore he does not take pride in it — rather, his intention in his offering is only toward Heaven alone. Likewise the wealthy person — even though he gives much to tzedakah — far be it from him to be boastful in the aspect of tzedakah and to intend in it for his own honor. Rather, even though he gives much to tzedakah — even so, in his own eyes he should be like a poor person. For in truth before Him, blessed be He, all are poor — as it is written: "Who can precede Me and I will pay him?" [Job 41:3]. For everything is only from Him, blessed be He. As it is written: "For everything is Yours and from Your hand we have given You" [I Chronicles 29:14]. And therefore King David, peace be upon him, at the time he gave much wealth for the donation toward the Temple said: "And now I have prepared with my poverty, etc." [I Chronicles 29:14] — for he considered all his giving as poverty. And such tzedakah is very precious — for it is the aspect of the minchas ani [offering of the poor] — which is very beloved because his intention is only toward Heaven with no self-glorification whatsoever. And therefore such tzedakah is called by the name minchah — in the aspect of: "those who offer a minchah in righteousness" [Malachi 3:3].

segments.he:
ז.
עקר מה שהשם יתברך מתפאר עם ישראל נגד כל האומות הוא על ידי דרכי התמימות שלהם האמתיים, וזה בחינת: ששים המה מלכות וכו', אחת היא יונתי תמתי - תמתי דיקא, בחינת תמימות. (שם, אות כב):
segments.en:
7.
The essential [means by which] G-d (blessed be He) takes glory in Israel before all the nations is through their true ways of temimus. And this is the aspect of: "There are sixty queens, etc. — one is she, my dove, my perfect one [tamasi]" — specifically tamasi — the aspect of temimus.

(ibid., item 22).

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One must give more tzedakah on the Festivals — in order to subdue the forehead [metzach] of the serpent and to reveal the forehead of will [metzach haratzon]. Through which one merits to hear the voice of the herald of Yom Tov — which calls out and reveals the will. Through which one merits the joy of Yom Tov. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said regarding Yom Tov: "If you gladden Mine — I will gladden yours." For through this one merits the joy of Yom Tov.

segments.he: תם ונשלם. שבח לאל בורא עולם:
segments.en: Completed and finished. Praise to G-d, Creator of the world.

history.en: Through tzedakah one appeases the burning heat of the heart that blazes toward the desire for sexual union and the desire for money — both of which depend upon one another, as explained in the inner teachings.

segments.he: סליק ספר עצות ישרות בעזרת רוכב שמים ומסדר המערכות:
segments.en: Concluded: the book Aitzoas Yeshuroas, with the help of the Rider of the heavens and the Arranger of the celestial orders.

history.en: Every single person of Israel — in the inner depth of his soul — yearns and burns very greatly for G-d. Because in the inner depth he gazes at all times toward the purpose [tachlis] — which is the light of the Infinite [ohr ha'ain sof] — from which his root derives. And he wishes to cleave and be encompassed there. But since this aspect is in the aspect of ratzo v'shov [advance and retreat] — and when he is in the aspect of shov [retreat], then the vessels of the expanded consciousness [kailim d'hamoi'ach] — which are the aspect of the garments — are unable to receive the light of the shining from there. And then most often the light of the impression [reshimah] of the nullification [bitul] is forgotten from him. And through the commandment of tzitzis — the garments are repaired. Which are the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the vessels of the expanded consciousness. So that they can receive the light of the shining of the impression from the nullification — from which is the root of all Torah. And this is the aspect of: "And you shall see it, etc." [Numbers 15:39] — whose essential [reference] is to the techeiles [blue dye] in the tzitzis. That is, one must look and gaze greatly upon the purpose [tachlis] — which is the aspect of techeiles — as explained in the inner teachings. And this: "and you shall not go astray after your hearts and after your eyes" — that he should close his eyes from the sight of this world entirely and direct his vision and his gaze only toward the purpose alone. "So that you shall remember and do all My commandments" [Numbers 15:40]. For through the commandment of tzitzis one merits to well remember the light of the impression aforementioned — from which flows the totality of Torah and commandments.

history.en: All the damagers of the world, G-d protect us — the essential nourishment they draw from is from evil longings and vanities. From which are made evil souls — which are those very damagers, G-d protect us. For they damage physically and spiritually — for they go and arouse people toward evil, G-d forbid. From which come all the damages, G-d protect us. And therefore the essential subduing and nullification [of these damagers] is through the Tzaddikim and the upright — who have good longings, which are the aspect of good souls. Which stir the world toward good. They are the ones who subdue and nullify all the damagers of the world — in the aspect of: "You shall tread upon the lion and the serpent, etc." [Psalms 91:13]. "Because he cleaves to Me, I will deliver him" [Psalms 91:14].

segments.en: Introduction

history.label: Earlier site English (historical comparison, not the current translation).
history.en: One must guard himself greatly — not to speak any evil word of evil longings and evil wills, G-d forbid, that come upon his heart. Rather, one should reverse the matter and train himself to speak always from his mouth good holy longings. Through which good effects are made in the world — and through this all the blessings and flows are drawn. And good souls are made — which go and circulate in the world and arouse the entire world toward G-d and His Torah.

segments.he:
ספר עצות ישרות מסודר על פי אלף בית מעט הכמות ורב האיכות. והמה אמרות טהורות. ודרך ישר לאדם יורות. להלך בהם לדורי דורות. אשר מכל דבר תבל היה נבדל. מפי הנשר הגדול. הלוא הוא הרב הקדוש, צדיק יסוד עולם, בוצינא קדישא איש אלקים מורנו ורבנו הרב רבי נתן זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה. והוא היה תלמיד מובהק של מורנו הרב רבי נחמן זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה, מברסלב. אשר השאיר השאיר אחריו ברכה על כל ארבעה חלקי שולחן ערוך, וקראם בשם לקוטי הלכות. ועתה האיר ה' את רוחי ולקטתי לקוטי בתר לקוטי מעט גרגרי חכמה ותבונה מספרי לקוטי הלכות הנ"ל ומספרי לקוטי מוהר"ן. להיותם לאחיזה ביד כל אדם, להיות להם לסולם לעלות במרומי מעלה במדרגות המדות הקדושות ועבודת השם: 
יסוד התשובה ומעלות ההתחזקות למלט נפשו משחת הוא לא בצומות וסיגופים, אלא לחזק באלו שלשה דברים: אהבת השם ואהבת ישראל ואהבת התורה, כמו שמבאר בספר "בוצינא דנהורא", שפעם אחת שאלו להבעל שם טוב, זכרונו לברכה, מהו עקר העבודה הלא אנו יודעים ואבותינו ספרו לנו, שבימים הקדמונים היו אנשי מעשה מתענין משבת לשבת, ואתם בטלתם את הדבר הזה, שאמרתם, שכל אדם שהוא מתענה עתיד לתן את הדין, שנקרא חוטא, שמענה את נפשו על כן הגידו נא לנו מה עקר העבודה. והשיב להם הבעל שם טוב, זכרונו לברכה: אני באתי לעולם הזה להראות דרך אחר, שיראה אדם להמשיך על עצמו שלשה דברים הללו, הינו: 
אהבת השם ואהבת ישראל ואהבת התורה, ואין צריך לעשות סגופים, עין שם עוד מענין זה: 
וכבר ידוע ומפורסם מקצה העולם ועד קצהו גדל קדושת אדוננו מורנו ורבנו, אור האורות וכו', הרב רבי נחמן, זכר צדיק לברכה, בעל המחבר הספרים הקדושים לקוטי מוהר"ן ושאר ספרים קדושים ונוראים מאד, ונראה לכל המעין בספריו הקדושים גדל עמקות עצותיו באהבת השם וכו'. והנה ביותר מכל תלמידיו הקדושים סמך ידיו על תלמידו הקדוש, הרב הצדיק רבי נתן, זכר צדיק לברכה, בעל המחבר הספרים הקדושים לקוטי הלכות ושאר ספרים קדושים. ועתה, בעקבא דמשיחא, שנתפשט החשכות הנורא מאד מאד, רחמנא לצלן, הן באמונת השם, הן באמונת הצדיקים, אשר גם נביאינו הראשונים, זכרונם לברכה, ראו כן תמהו, איך יוכלו בני ישראל הקדושים להתחזק ביראת השם בתוך החשכות הנורא הזה, כמצינו בכמה מקומות, ומבאר בזהר הקדוש וזה לשונו: רבי שמעון זקף ידו ובכה ואמר: וי מאן דיזדמן בההוא זמנא, וזכאה חולקא מאן דיזדמן וישתכח בההוא זמנא. וי מאן דיזדמן בההוא זמנא בגין דכד ייתי קודשא בריך הוא לפקדא לאילתא, יסתכל מאן אנון דקימין בהדה, בכל אנון דמשתכחין עמה, בכל עובדוי דכל חד וחד, ולא ישתכח זכאי, דכתיב: ואביט ואין עוזר, וכמה עקתין על עקתין לישראל. זכאה מאן דיזדמן וישתכח בההוא זמנא, בגין דההוא דיתקים בההוא זמנא בהמנותא, יזכה לההוא נהירו דחדוה דמלכא וכו', עין שם. וגם מבאר בדברי חכמינו זכרונם לברכה, במסכת סוטה: רבי אליעזר הגדול אומר: מיום שחרב בית חמדתנו שרי חכימיא למהוי כספריא וכו', חוצפא יסגי ויקר יאמיר וכו', וחכמת סופרים תסרח, ויראי חטא ימאסו, והאמת תהא נעדרת, נערים ילבינו זקנים, גדולים יעמדו מפני הקטנים וכו', עין שם. ברוך השם, אשר הקדים רפואה למכתנו, ושלח לנו מושיע, נחל נובע, הוא אדוננו מורנו ורבנו הקדוש, זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה, אשר הוא ותלמידו הקדוש, זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה, הודיעו לנו רב רחמנותו של הקדוש ברוך הוא עלינו עד אין חקר, אך דבריהם הקדושים והתחזקויותם העצומים מפוזרים בהתורות הקדושים, שבספרי ה"לקוטי מוהר"ן" ובספרי ה"לקוטי הלכות", וראה ראיתי, אשר עתה בתקף הגלות והחשכות, בעקבא דמשיחא, יש רבים מאחינו בני ישראל, שמשתוקקים מאד לעבודת השם, אך נדמה להם, כי אין להם תקוה, חס ושלום. לזאת באתי, אנכי הצעיר, ולקטתי וקבצתי דברי ההתחזקות, שנדפסו בספרים הקדושים "לקוטי מוהר"ן" ובספרי "לקוטי הלכות" ומספר "לקוטי עצות החדש", שחבר הרב הקדוש מטשערין, זכר צדיק לברכה, ועוד משאר ספרים הקדושים, להדפיסם בכרך הקטן הזה, למען יוכל כל איש לרוות נפשו הצמאה, וידע, אשר עדין לא אבדה תקותו, חלילה: 
וקראתי שם הספר עצות ישרות, והמה עצות נכונות בדרכי השם, והתחזקות נפלאה להמשיך על עצמו שלשת הדברים הנ"ל, ולהתעורר בהם לראות, שאין שום יאוש בעולם, ואפלו אם נפל כמו שנפל, רחמנא לצלן, אוף על פי כן השם אתו, כמובא ב"לקוטי הלכות", הלכות נטילת ידים, הלכה ו', אות פב. ורשמתי אצל כל אות ואות שבחבר הזה מקור מוצאו, ואם ירצה המעין לעין, יעין שם ויבין הענין בשלמות יותר. וסדרתי אותם על פי אלף בית. ונזכה לקימו באמת, עד שנזכה לשוב בתשובה שלמה, לעשות רצון השם בלב שלם אמן, כן יהי רצון:
segments.en:
The book Aitzoas Yeshuroas is arranged according to the Alef-Bais — small in quantity and abundant in quality. And they are pure utterances. And they instruct a person in a straight path. To walk in them for generations upon generations. From the mouth of the great eagle, who was separated from every worldly matter. Who is none other than the holy Rav, the Tzadik, yesod olam [foundation of the world], the holy luminary, the man of G-d, our teacher and master, Rav Nassan, of blessed, saintly and holy memory. And he was the foremost disciple of our teacher and master, Rav Nachman of Breslov, of blessed, saintly and holy memory. [Rav Nassan] left behind — [left behind] — after him a blessing over all four sections of the Shulchan Aruch, and called them by the name Likutay Halachos. And now G-d has illuminated my spirit, and I gleaned — gleanings after gleanings — a few kernels of wisdom and understanding from the books of Likutay Halachos aforementioned, and from the books of Likutay Moharan. So that they may serve as a handhold for every person, to be for them a ladder by which to ascend to the heights above, rung by rung through the holy character traits and the service of G-d.

The foundation of teshuvah and the great virtue of hischazakus [strengthening oneself] — to rescue one's soul from the pit — is not through fasting and self-mortification, but rather to strengthen oneself in these three things: love of G-d, and love of Israel, and love of Torah. As it is explained in the book Botzina d'Nehora, that once they asked the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory: What is the essential avodah [service]? — for we know, and our fathers have told us, that in former times men of great deeds would fast from Shabbos to Shabbos, and you have abolished this practice, saying that whoever fasts will in the future have to give an accounting, and is called a sinner for having afflicted his soul — therefore tell us please, what is the essential service? And the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, replied to them: I came into this world to show a different path — that a person should strive to draw upon himself these three things, namely:

Love of G-d, and love of Israel, and love of Torah — and there is no need to do mortifications. See there for more on this topic.

And it is already known and famous from one end of the world to the other — the greatness of the holiness of our master, teacher, and rebbe, the light of lights, etc. — Rav Nachman, of righteous memory, the author of the holy books Likutay Moharan and other exceedingly holy and awesome works. And it is apparent to all who study his holy books — the great depth of his counsels regarding love of G-d, etc. And behold, more than all his other holy disciples, he leaned his hands upon his holy disciple, the Rav and Tzadik Rav Nassan, of righteous memory, the author of the holy books Likutay Halachos and other holy works. And now, in the ikvesa d'Meshicha [footsteps of the Messiah], when the dreadful darkness has spread — exceedingly, exceedingly — Heaven protect us, both in faith in G-d and in faith in the Tzaddikim. Even our earliest prophets, of blessed memory, saw such a time and were astonished — how would the holy Children of Israel be able to strengthen themselves in the fear of G-d within this terrible darkness? As we find in many places. And the holy Zohar explains this, and these are its words:

Rabbi Shimon raised his hand and wept and said: "Woe to him who is present in that time, and yet — fortunate is the portion of one who is present and is found in that time. Woe to him who is present in that time, for when the Holy One, blessed be He, comes to visit the gazelle [the Shechinah], He will look at who stands with her, at all those found with her, at the deeds of each and every one — and no righteous person will be found, as it is written: I looked and there was no helper, and how many troubles upon troubles for Israel. Fortunate is the one who is present and is found in that time, for the one who stands firm in that time with faith will merit that light of the joy of the King, etc." — see there.

And likewise it is explained in the words of our Sages of blessed memory, in tractate Sotah:

"Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: From the day the Temple of our delight was destroyed, the wise began to become like scribes, etc. — insolence will multiply and prices will soar, etc. — and the wisdom of the scribes will become putrid, and those who fear sin will be despised, and truth will be absent, youths will shame elders, the great ones will rise before the small ones, etc." — see there.

Blessed be G-d, who preceded the healing to our wound, and sent us a savior — a Nachal Novea [ever-flowing, gushing stream] — who is our master, teacher, and holy rebbe, of blessed, saintly and holy memory. He and his holy disciple, of blessed, saintly and holy memory, made known to us the boundless compassion of the Holy One, blessed be He, over us — beyond any reckoning. Yet their holy words and their tremendous words of encouragement are scattered throughout the holy Torah teachings in the books of Likutay Moharan and in the books of Likutay Halachos. And I saw — [indeed saw] — that now at the height of the exile and the darkness, in the footsteps of the Messiah, there are many of our brethren the Children of Israel who yearn deeply for the service of G-d, but it appears to them that they have no hope, G-d forbid. Therefore I came — I, the young one [hatzair] — and I gleaned and gathered the words of encouragement that were printed in the holy books Likutay Moharan, and in the books of Likutay Halachos, and from the book Likutay Aitzoas HaChadash composed by the holy Rav from Tcherin, of righteous memory, and from other holy books besides — to print them in this small volume, so that every person may be able to satisfy his thirsting soul, and know that his hope has not yet perished — G-d forbid.

And I called the name of this book Aitzoas Yeshuroas — and they are proper counsels in the ways of G-d, and a wondrous strengthening — to draw upon oneself the three aforementioned things, and to be awakened within them to see that there is no despair in the world whatsoever, and even if one has fallen however he has fallen, G-d protect us — even so, G-d is with him, as is brought in Likutay Halachos, Hilchos Netilas Yadayim, Halacha 6, item 82. And I noted alongside each and every item of this work its source of origin — and if the reader wishes to look further, let him look there and he will understand the matter more fully. And I arranged them according to the Alef-Bais. And may we merit to fulfill them in truth, until we merit to return in complete teshuvah, to do the will of G-d with a full heart — Amen, so may it be His will.
